title: Parasitic Infections of the Lacrimal System: A Major Review of Etiology, Clinical Presentation, and Management.
abstract: Purpose Parasitic infections of the lacrimal system are rare and often under-recognized causes of lacrimal pathology. Their clinical presentation frequently mimics more common conditions such as chronic dacryocystitis, leading to diagnostic challenges and delays in appropriate management. This study aims to systematically review the literature on parasitic infections of the lacrimal system and to characterize their etiology, clinical presentation, diagnostic approaches, management strategies, and outcomes. Methods A systematic review was conducted across MEDLINE, Embase, Emcare, and PubMed from inception to March 2026. Studies reporting parasitic infections involving the lacrimal apparatus were included. Data on demographics, clinical presentation, anatomical involvement, causative organisms, diagnostic methods, treatment, and outcomes were extracted. Due to heterogeneity and predominance of case reports and small series, a qualitative descriptive analysis was performed. Results A total of 44 studies comprising 172 cases were included. Rhinosporidium seeberi was the most frequently reported pathogen, accounting for 147 cases (85.5%), followed by Leishmania (8 cases, 4.7%) and Ascaris lumbricoides (7 cases, 4.1%). The lacrimal sac was the most commonly involved site. Clinical presentation was nonspecific, with epiphora and medial canthal swelling predominating. Diagnosis was most often established by histopathology following surgical intervention. Management varied by etiology, with surgical excision commonly used for rhinosporidiosis and mechanical extraction for helminthic infections. Outcomes were generally favorable, although recurrence was reported, particularly in R. seeberi infections. Conclusions Parasitic infections of the lacrimal system are rare but clinically important, with diverse presentations and management approaches. Increased awareness is essential for early diagnosis and appropriate treatment. Further studies with standardized reporting are needed to optimize management strategies.

title: Lactation Management in Patients With Cancer: An Evidence-Based Framework for Surgical Practice.
abstract: BackgroundThe coexistence of lactation and cancer care, termed oncolactation , is becoming increasingly common as childbearing is delayed and more women are diagnosed with malignancy during the reproductive years. However, evidence-based guidance regarding breastfeeding during oncologic evaluation and treatment remains fragmented, particularly for surgeons involved in multidisciplinary cancer care.MethodsWe conducted a narrative review with a systematic literature search using PubMed/MEDLINE and professional society guidelines (American Society of Breast Surgeons (ASBrS), American College of Radiology (ACR), American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists (ACOG), and the Drugs and Lactation Database (LactMed®). Publications addressing surgical management, diagnostic imaging, systemic therapy, radiation therapy, and reproductive counseling in lactating patients with cancer were critically synthesized to develop practical, evidence-based recommendations.ResultsMost diagnostic and surgical interventions-including mammography, breast MRI, computed tomography, image-guided biopsy, and general anesthesia-are compatible with continued breastfeeding when appropriate precautions are observed. Cytotoxic chemotherapy, endocrine therapy, and most targeted or immunotherapeutic agents remain contraindicated because of insufficient safety data or potential infant toxicity. Radiation therapy generally precludes breastfeeding from the treated breast, but permits continued feeding from the contralateral breast. Emerging evidence also supports individualized counseling regarding fertility preservation, future pregnancy, and survivorship.ConclusionsOncolactation should be incorporated into routine surgical oncology practice. Most surgical and diagnostic procedures can be performed without interrupting breastfeeding, whereas systemic therapies require individualized pharmacologic assessment. Integration of evidence-based lactation guidance into multidisciplinary cancer care promotes safe, patient-centered decision-making while maintaining oncologic safety and supporting breastfeeding whenever feasible.

title: Symptomatic Superior Vena Cava Lipoma Causing Near-Complete Venous Obstruction: A Case Report and Literature Review.
abstract: BackgroundLipomas are common benign mesenchymal tumors; however, intravascular localization is exceedingly rare. Superior vena cava (SVC) involvement represents an exceptional entity, with only a limited number of cases reported in the literature. Intravascular lipomas are frequently detected incidentally but may present with symptoms related to venous obstruction, including superior vena cava syndrome. We report a rare case of SVC-origin intravascular lipoma extending into the right brachiocephalic vein, accompanied by a focused review of previously published upper extremity cases.Case PresentationA 77-year-old male presented with facial and cervical edema, dyspnea exacerbated in the supine position, and distended cervical veins. Contrast-enhanced computed tomography revealed a 5-cm elongated, fat-attenuation mass within the SVC extending into the right brachiocephalic vein, causing near-total (approximately 99%) luminal occlusion. title: Why clinicians in acute hospitals may fail to engage in direct communication with people with intellectual disability.
abstract: This case highlights the healthcare inequities faced by people with intellectual disability, including diagnostic overshadowing, communication barriers, and the need for personalised, meaningful adjustments in care. A woman in her fifties with mild intellectual disability, epilepsy, and diabetes insipidus experienced delayed diagnosis and treatment because healthcare providers assumed she could not tolerate magnetic resonance imaging; however, when the scan was eventually completed with supported communication, it revealed a serious brain tumour with metastases. The case shows that diagnostic overshadowing can arise not only from misattributing symptoms, but also from untested assumptions about a patient's ability to engage with diagnostic procedures. It also underscores the importance of involving patients and families directly in healthcare decisions to support autonomy and prevent avoidable harm. Addressing these systemic issues is essential to deliver equitable, patient-centred care in acute hospital settings.

title: Computed tomography angiography with three-dimensional reconstruction for planning aortic valve replacement via right anterior mini-thoracotomy.
abstract: Introduction This study explored the value of computed tomography angiography (CTA) with three-dimensional (3D) reconstruction in aortic valve replacement (AVR) via right anterior mini-thoracotomy. Methods Clinical data were retrospectively collected from 168 patients who underwent AVR at our institution in China between 1 July 2018 and 1 September 2022. After 1:1 propensity score matching, the experimental group (right anterior mini-thoracotomy) and control group (median sternotomy) each comprised 43 patients. Patients in the experimental group underwent preoperative aortic CTA with 3D reconstruction to guide individualised selection of the intercostal incision site. Perioperative and clinical outcomes were compared between groups. Results The experimental group had significantly lower 24-hour postoperative drainage volume and shorter mechanical ventilation time, intensive care unit stay, and total hospital stay than the control group (all P<0.001). No intraoperative conversion to median sternotomy or postoperative reoperation for bleeding or pericardial tamponade occurred in the experimental group. Postoperatively, five patients (11.6%) developed atelectasis or pulmonary infection, five (11.6%) developed pleural effusion, and five (11.6%) developed subcutaneous emphysema or pneumothorax; none required thoracentesis. Aortic cross-clamping and cardiopulmonary bypass times were approximately 8 minutes longer, respectively, in the experimental group. At 24 months, the incidence of the composite endpoint-including all-cause mortality, cardiocerebrovascular complications, and readmission for massive pleural effusion or coagulation dysfunction-did not differ significantly between groups. Conclusion Preoperative CTA with 3D reconstruction enables accurate localisation of the right intercostal incision for AVR via right anterior mini-thoracotomy. This technique preserves minimally invasive surgery benefits and does not increase risks of mid/long-term adverse events.

title: Brain Tumour Detection Using EfficientNet-Transformer Hybrid Network with SHAP and Grad-CAM Based Explainable Artificial Intelligence
abstract: Accurate and interpretable brain tumour detection from magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) remains a significant challenge in computer-aided diagnosis. This study proposes an EfficientNet–Transformer Hybrid Network integrated with SHapley Additive ExPlanations (SHAP) and Grad-CAM explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) techniques for automated and trustworthy brain tumour classification. Methods: The proposed framework combines EfficientNet for local feature extraction and a Vision Transformer for global contextual learning. MRI images from publicly available benchmark datasets containing four classes (glioma, meningioma, pituitary tumour, and no tumour) were preprocessed and augmented before training. The model was trained using an 80:20 training-testing split, while SHAP and Grad-CAM were employed to provide feature-level and spatial explanations of predictions. Results: The proposed framework achieved a classification accuracy of 98.88%, outperforming several state-of-the-art CNN and transformer models. It also attained average precision, recall, and F1-score values of 98.90%, 98.88%, and 98.89%, respectively, with an average AUC of 0.9893. Ablation and robustness analyses demonstrated that integrating SHAP and Grad-CAM improved interpretability while maintaining high predictive performance under noisy conditions. Conclusions: The proposed EfficientNet–Transformer framework effectively combines local and global feature learning with dual explainability mechanisms to deliver accurate and clinically interpretable brain tumour classification. The results demonstrate its potential as a reliable computer-aided diagnosis tool for neuro-oncology and clinical decision support systems.

title: Beyond the Classical Paradigm of Diabetic Kidney Disease (DKD): Evolving Phenotypes and the Role of Kidney Biopsy
abstract: Diabetic kidney disease (DKD) is increasingly recognized as a heterogeneous condition encompassing distinct clinical and pathological phenotypes. Albuminuria and estimated glomerular filtration rate may follow divergent trajectories, with non-albuminuric kidney function decline representing a common and clinically relevant phenotype. Importantly, clinical features do not always reflect the underlying renal pathology, as patients with diabetes may present with diabetic kidney disease, non-diabetic kidney disease (NDKD), or mixed lesions. Conventional clinical markers, including diabetic retinopathy, hematuria, proteinuria, and eGFR decline, modify but do not reliably establish the underlying diagnosis. Kidney biopsy therefore retains a selective but important role in patients with atypical or rapidly evolving presentations, particularly when histological findings may alter treatment or prognosis. Beyond diagnostic classification, biopsy can provide prognostic information through assessment of glomerular, tubulointerstitial, and vascular injury. Future approaches should integrate longitudinal clinical trajectories with histopathology and molecular profiling, positioning kidney biopsy as a bridge toward mechanism-based classification and precision medicine in DKD.

title: Binary Classification of Breast Cancer Images Using CNNs Enhanced by ALO-CLAHE-MSER Preprocessing
abstract: This work presents an intelligent image-processing framework for automatically detecting and clas-sifying benign and malignant regions in breast tissue by integrating Contrast Limited Adaptive His-togram Equalization (CLAHE), Maximally Stable Extremal Regions (MSER), and metaheuristic opti-mization algorithms. Identifying tumor-related regions in breast images is challenging because their visual characteristics can vary considerably with tissue density, illumination conditions, surface tex-ture, intensity distribution, lesion severity, and image acquisition conditions. These variations can make conventional image segmentation and manually configured MSER approaches sensitive to pa-rameter selection and less robust when detecting heterogeneous cancerous regions. To address these limitations, this study highlights the critical role of metaheuristic optimization as a key driver for fully automating and optimizing the combined CLAHE-MSER pipeline for binary breast cancer classifica-tion. Methods: First, CLAHE is applied to the input medical images to improve local contrast and enhance visual differences between healthy and cancerous tissue. The enhanced images are subse-quently processed using the MSER technique to identify stable intensity regions potentially associated with lesions or tumor masses. Rather than relying on manual configuration, the MSER parameter space and enhancement thresholds are formulated as a multidimensional optimization problem, and metaheuristic optimization algorithms are employed to automatically explore the parameter space and determine optimal configurations for region detection. Candidate solutions are iteratively evalu-ated using an objective function designed to improve the quality, stability, spatial coherence, and ac-curacy of the detected tumor regions prior to binary classification. The proposed metaheuristic-driven CLAHE-MSER framework therefore lets the detection process adapt automatically to the visual char-acteristics of individual medical images while eliminating dependence on manually selected parame-ters. Results: We performed experimental evaluations on medical images containing healthy, benign, and malignant regions. We quantitatively evaluated the performance of the proposed CLAHE-MSER framework, optimized by metaheuristic algorithms, using several image-quality, region-detection, and binary classification metrics. The experimental results indicate that incorporating CLAHE improves local contrast and facilitates the identification of subtle differences between healthy and affected tis-sue. Furthermore, metaheuristic optimization significantly improves MSER parameter selection, re-sulting in more consistent and spatially coherent detection of tumor regions than conventional MSER configurations and non-optimized approaches. The optimized configurations better preserve relevant cancer-related structures, maximizing overall binary classification accuracy while drastically reduc-ing the detection of healthy tissue and irrelevant regions. Conclusion: Integrating CLAHE- MSER, and metaheuristic optimization provides a robust, fully automated, and adaptive framework for binary breast cancer classification based on medical image analysis. CLAHE enhances the visual infor-mation needed to distinguish affected tissue, while MSER extracts stable image regions associated with potential tumor lesions. Metaheuristic optimization serves as the central component to automate and refine the detection process by dynamically identifying suitable parameter configurations for different image conditions. The proposed methodology represents a promising computational ap-proach for automated breast cancer screening, computer-aided diagnosis (CAD), lesion classification, and intelligent medical decision support systems.

title: A Systematic Review and Descriptive Quantitative Synthesis of Artificial Intelligence in Cervical Cancer Screening and Diagnosis
abstract: Abstract Artificial intelligence (AI) has been frequently utilised in cervical cancer screening, diagnosis, lesion assessment and clinical decision support, but the evidence remains methodologically heterogeneous. This systematic review examined the application of AI in cytology, colposcopy, visual examination, histopathology, and multimodal clinical data. Also reviewed PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science and IEEE Xplore to identify 4094 records. After the exclusion of 2053 duplicates and applying pre-defined eligibility criteria, 898 studies were included. Directly extractable diagnostic-performance measures were available from 60 studies. Accuracy was reported in 40 studies, sensitivity in 19, specificity in 16 and AUC in 12 studies. A total of 13 studies reported both sensitivity and specificity. There was considerable heterogeneity in populations, datasets, reference standards, diagnostic tasks, AI methods, validation procedures and performance reporting. Complete TP, FP, TN and FN data were not available across the eligible evidence base and pooled diagnostic accuracy estimation and summary receiver-operating-characteristic analysis were not possible. Therefore, the quantitative results were summarized descriptively. Evidence indicates broad application of AI approaches but also limitations in terms of comparability, external validation, reporting completeness and clinical generalizability. Future research should focus on standardized reporting, multicenter datasets, independent external validation and prospective clinical evaluation.

title: An acoustic coupling fluid improves intraoperative ultrasound image quality during glioma surgery: Results of a Pivotal Multicenter Study (NCT04734444)
abstract: Abstract Intraoperative ultrasound uniquely provides repeatable, real-time guidance throughout glioma resection without interrupting surgery. However, image quality deteriorates at resection completion, when imaging is most critical: irrigation fluids attenuate ultrasound less than brain tissue, producing hyperechoic artefacts beneath the cavity that obscure or mimic residual tumour. Existing operator-dependent strategies do not correct this mismatch. Here, we show that SonoClear, a tissue-mimicking acoustic coupling fluid, reduces these artefacts and improves interpretability. In a prospective, non-randomised study at five centres, 44 patients received SonoClear and 40 contributed to paired comparisons with standard irrigation fluid. SonoClear reduced below-cavity artefactual signal (ratio of contrast-to-noise ratios, irrigation/SonoClear: 1.70; 95% CI, 1.48–1.95). Five independent neurosurgeons masked to the fluid reported a mean paired Surgeon Image Rating improvement of 1.96 points (95% CI, 1.80–2.11). No serious adverse events were judged probably or definitely device-related within 30 days; postoperative magnetic resonance imaging showed no major findings in 36 evaluated patients. These findings support acoustic matching to improve ultrasound guidance, including at resection completion; effects on resection extent and patient outcomes require investigation.

title: Successful emicizumab prophylaxis in treatment-refractory acquired von Willebrand syndrome associated with rheumatoid arthritis
abstract: Abstract Acquired von Willebrand syndrome (AVWS) is a rare bleeding disorder characterized by acquired quantitative or qualitative abnormalities of von Willebrand factor (VWF) and may occur in association with autoimmune disease. Management can be challenging when conventional hemostatic and immunomodulatory therapies fail. We report a 63-year-old man with longstanding rheumatoid arthritis (RA) and no personal or family history of abnormal bleeding who developed life-threatening hemorrhage following dental extractions, resulting in airway obstruction requiring tracheostomy and red blood cell transfusion. Evaluation demonstrated an isolated prolonged activated partial thromboplastin time, markedly reduced factor VIII (FVIII) activity, profoundly decreased VWF antigen and activity, and no detectable FVIII inhibitor. The late onset of bleeding, negative genetic testing, poor VWF recovery following high-dose VWF/FVIII concentrate, and underlying autoimmune disease supported a diagnosis of AVWS. Severe VWF deficiency persisted despite treatment with rituximab, methotrexate, and intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIG). Emicizumab was subsequently initiated for prophylactic hemostasis. The patient remained free of spontaneous bleeding despite persistent severe reductions in VWF and FVIII measurements and subsequently underwent upper endoscopy with biopsy and colonoscopy without hemorrhagic complications using adjunctive tranexamic acid. To our knowledge, this represents the first reported case of RA-associated AVWS successfully managed with emicizumab prophylaxis. This case demonstrates sustained clinical hemostasis with emicizumab in treatment-refractory AVWS associated with RA and supports further investigation of FVIII-mimetic therapy as a potential prophylactic strategy when conventional therapies are ineffective.

title: Synoptic procedural reporting to improve quality indicators in systematic Staging Endobronchial Ultrasound (EBUS) in Non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC): protocol for an ambispective multi-centre quality improvement study
abstract: Abstract Background: Accurate mediastinal staging by systematic staging endobronchial ultrasound (EBUS) is essential for prognosticating and guiding management in curative-intent treatment in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). Narrative procedural reports are often incomplete and inconsistent between clinicians, limiting assessment of procedural quality and meaningful audit. Synoptic (structured, check-list style) reporting has improved documentation completeness and procedural quality in other domains of medicine, and a recent Australian multicentre study demonstrated synoptic reporting significantly improved both report and procedural quality in staging EBUS. This ambispective, international, multicentre study aims to evaluate whether synoptic procedural reporting improves quality indicators of systematic staging EBUS, encompassing both process and outcome measures, and will assess acceptability and feasibility to proceduralists. Methods: This ambispective multicentre, single-arm interventional study will recruit approximately 15 lung cancer services with substantial EBUS procedural volume. Eligible patients will have known or suspected clinical stage IB-IIIC NSCLC undergoing systematic staging EBUS for treatment planning. Each centre will implement a mandated synoptic report requiring documentation for each of the five mediastinal lymph nodes: examination, size of node and biopsy details. Three months of staging procedures will be contributed prior to and following implementation of this reporting practice. The primary outcome is the proportion of patients with a complete staging procedure. Secondary outcomes include PET-occult lymph node metastases detection, nodes sampled, radiologically normal node sampling, inter-site variance, and proceduralist feasibility/acceptability. A sample of 590 patients (295 pre-, 295 post-intervention) provides 80% power to detect an 8% increase in complete staging. Mixed-effects logistic and Poisson regression, with random effect for centre and adjustment for pre-specified baseline case-mix covariates, will be used. Discussion: This study will provide the first international multicentre evaluation of whether synoptic reporting improves procedural completeness and clinically meaningful outcomes in systematic staging EBUS. Demonstrating improved complete staging procedures and PET-occult lymph node detection, with proceduralist acceptability, would support widespread adoption of synoptic reporting as a quality improvement tool, strengthen alignment with WABIP quality frameworks, reduce variance in care, and support more accurate multidisciplinary decision-making for NSCLC patients. Trial registration: Australian New Zealand Clinical Trials Registry (ANZCTR), ACTRN12625001281482. Registered 18 November 2025. Retrospectively registered.

Eligible patients will have known or suspected clinical stage IB-IIIC NSCLC undergoing systematic staging EBUS for treatment planning. Each centre will implement a mandated synoptic report requiring documentation for each of the five mediastinal lymph nodes: examination, size of node and biopsy details. Three months of staging procedures will be contributed prior to and following implementation of this reporting practice. The primary outcome is the proportion of patients with a complete staging procedure. Secondary outcomes include PET-occult lymph node metastases detection, nodes sampled, radiologically normal node sampling, inter-site variance, and proceduralist feasibility/acceptability. A sample of 590 patients (295 pre-, 295 post-intervention) provides 80% power to detect an 8% increase in complete staging. Mixed-effects logistic and Poisson regression, with random effect for centre and adjustment for pre-specified baseline case-mix covariates, will be used. Discussion: This study will provide the first international multicentre evaluation of whether synoptic reporting improves procedural completeness and clinically meaningful outcomes in systematic staging EBUS. Demonstrating improved complete staging procedures and PET-occult lymph node detection, with proceduralist acceptability, would support widespread adoption of synoptic reporting as a quality improvement tool, strengthen alignment with WABIP quality frameworks, reduce variance in care, and support more accurate multidisciplinary decision-making for NSCLC patients. title: From detection to decision: radiographic predictors of clinical complications in 514 supernumerary teeth: A retrospective cross-sectional study
abstract: Abstract Background Supernumerary teeth exhibit various morphological characteristics and may lead to a range of complications. This study aimed to evaluate radiographic characteristics of supernumerary teeth in children and to determine associations with complications and treatment status. Materials and methods This study included 386 systemically healthy paediatric patients (5–15.9 years) with 514 supernumerary teeth identified on panoramic radiographs. Variables included number, location, morphology, eruption direction, eruption status, root development stage, and complications. Statistical analyses included chi-square tests, independent samples t-tests, and multivariable binary logistic and multinomial regression models. Results The mean age was 9.07 ± 2.08 years, and 70.2% of patients were male. Significant differences were observed between erupted and impacted teeth regarding morphology, eruption direction, root development stage, complications, and Cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) use (p < 0.05). Morphology and root development stage were associated with complication patterns (p < 0.05). Multivariable regression analyses showed that CBCT use was associated with eruption status, dentition “stage, side distribution, and delayed eruption. Anterior maxillary localisation was strongly associated with conical and tuberculate morphologies. Midline location was associated with increased odds of both complete and partial root development (p < 0.001). Conclusion Supernumerary teeth exhibit distinct radiographic characteristics associated with clinical complications. Morphology, eruption status, and root development were associated with clinical and radiographic findings. Early radiographic evaluation is essential for individualised treatment planning.

title: Functional and MRI improvement followed by a mixed trajectory during cannabinoid-terpenoid exposure in glioblastoma: a case report
abstract: Abstract Background: Glioblastoma has limited salvage options, while viable tumour, treatment injury, postoperative change, oedema and corticosteroid effects may produce overlapping clinical and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) findings. Materials and Methods: Clinical records, serial MRI examinations and signed radiology reports were reviewed descriptively for a patient with IDH-wildtype, MGMT-promoter-methylated glioblastoma. The exposure history and contemporaneously documented neurological findings were aligned with seven MRI time points. No blinded central review, standardised volumetry or formal RANO 2.0 adjudication was performed. Results: After two operations, radiotherapy, concomitant temozolomide and three adjuvant cycles, serial MRI documented progression before April 2025. During a non-standard exposure state comprising intranasal perillyl alcohol and alpha-bisabolol, individualised cannabinoids and docosahexaenoic acid/medium-chain triglyceride oil, with dexamethasone fixed at 2 mg/day, hemiplegia/KPS 50 improved to hemiparesis with regained walking/KPS 80, coinciding with reduced enhancement. Later MRI showed increasing right temporal and cerebellar enhancement, including a new contralateral cerebellar focus, despite substantially stable postoperative cavity and T2/FLAIR extent. June 2026 lesion perfusion curves were low-amplitude without pathological hyperperfusion. The patient subsequently died after an overall survival of 45 months. Conclusions: This uncontrolled case documents early functional and radiological improvement on a stable corticosteroid background, followed by an anatomically progressive but biologically indeterminate trajectory. It does not establish treatment causality, survival benefit, formal tumour response or component-specific efficacy; mixed viable tumour and treatment effect or radiation necrosis could not be excluded. Although this single case does not establish a verified benefit the observed overall survival reached a time span of extraordinarily 45 months.

title: Neural correlates of empathy in autism: a coordinate-based meta-analysis
abstract: Abstract Purpose . Autistic and non-autistic people often differ in how readily they understand one another’s intentions and emotional states. Although empathy is commonly invoked to explain these differences, which components of empathic processing differ in autism, and their neural underpinnings, remain unclear. Methods . We conducted a pre-registered coordinate-based meta-analysis (activation likelihood estimation; ALE) of task-based fMRI studies of empathy in autism, examining within-group convergence, conjunction and between-group divergence separately for affective and cognitive components. Eleven studies (12 independent samples) met inclusion criteria, comprising 213 autistic and 216 non-autistic participants and 600 foci across 35 experiments; a multi-agent AI second reviewer supported screening and extraction. Results . Both groups shared a core empathy network (precuneus/posterior cingulate cortex, right middle temporal gyrus/posterior superior temporal sulcus, left inferior frontal gyrus, dorsomedial paracingulate), but the rostral dorsomedial prefrontal cortex, a canonical cognitive-empathy hub, converged only in non-autistic participants. The between-group contrast was strongly asymmetric: non-autistic participants exceeded autistic convergence in ten regions, eight of them cognitive-empathy nodes, the largest in rostral dorsomedial prefrontal cortex; autistic participants exceeded non-autistic convergence in one region only, the posterior right temporoparietal junction. Subdomain analyses indicated relatively preserved convergence for affective empathy, with sparser, more diffuse overlap for cognitive empathy. Conclusion . These findings are consistent with a dissociation between relatively preserved affective and altered cognitive empathy in autism, and suggest a redistribution of activation within the mentalizing network rather than a global absence of empathy-related processing. Key words: autism spectrum disorder; empathy; activation likelihood estimation; functional magnetic resonance imaging; dorsomedial prefrontal cortex; temporoparietal junction

title: Clinical and radiological comparisons of posterior labral tears with and without posterior glenohumeral instability.
abstract: Background We compare clinical and radiological characteristics and evaluate surgical outcomes of posterior labral tears based on the presence of glenohumeral instability. Methods Patients who were unresponsive to conservative treatment and underwent arthroscopic posterior labral repair were reviewed retrospectively. Patients were divided into two groups: those with glenohumeral instability (group 1) and those without (group 2). Demographic, radiological, physical examination, and intraoperative data were collected. Clinical outcomes were assessed at a minimum 2-year follow-up using the visual analog scale for pain, American Shoulder and Elbow Surgeons, and Rowe scores. Results The study included a total of 85 patients (40 in group 1 and 45 in group 2) with a mean follow-up duration of 31.8±12.2 months. Patients in group 2 were older (31.4±1.0 years old, P<0.001), had longer symptom durations (30.1±5.6 months, P=0.002), and included fewer histories of trauma (16 patients, P=0.009). Competitive sports were more common in group 1 (9 patients, P=0.005), whereas weightlifting exercises were more common in group 2 (24 patients, P=0.047). Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) underestimated incomplete posterior labral tears more frequently in group 2 than in group 1 (P=0.033). The incidence of arthroscopically detected tears among MRI-occult tears was higher in group 2 (10 patients) than in group 1 (2 patients, P=0.029). Statistically significant improvements in shoulder function were observed postoperatively in both groups. Conclusions Clinical and magnetic resonance findings of posterior labral tears without glenohumeral instability differ from those with instability. Surgical treatment achieved satisfactory clinical outcomes regardless of the presence of instability. Level of evidence: III.

title: FreqFuseNet: Scale-Normalized Dual-Frequency Fusion for Thin-Wall Head-and-Neck OAR Segmentation
abstract: Accurate segmentation of thin-wall organs-at-risk (OARs) in head-and-neck computed tomography (CT) is challenging because small contour deviations can substantially affect boundary agreement. We present FreqFuseNet, a segmentation architecture with a fast Fourier transform (FFT) primary branch and a frequency channel attention network (FcaNet) residual branch that explicitly aligns heterogeneous frequency-feature scales before bounded residual fusion. An initialization-time analysis revealed an approximately 863-fold activation-scale disparity between the two branches, corresponding to an approximately 43-fold unintended residual-to-primary magnitude ratio under naive fusion with a nominal coefficient of 0.05. FreqFuseNet uses per-sample, per-channel scale alignment to preserve the intended relative amplitude without additional normalization parameters. We evaluated 10 thin-wall OARs on SegRap2023 (84 training, 18 validation, and 18 testing CT cases) under a standardized binary per-OAR region-of-interest (ROI) protocol. In two training seeds, FreqFuseNet achieved Dice of 0.849 and 0.843, 95th-percentile Hausdorff distance (HD95) of 0.824 and 0.823 mm, and surface Dice at 1 mm of 0.959 and 0.957. In case-level paired comparisons for the primary seed (Wilcoxon signed-rank test, not corrected for multiple comparisons), FreqFuseNet showed significant improvements over 3D U-Net and MedNeXt-S, whereas differences versus an alternative learned fusion design (FixedFusion) and SegResNet were not statistically significant. These findings identify a practical feature-scale calibration issue in dual-frequency segmentation and demonstrate competitive boundary-sensitive performance of the proposed architecture within the evaluated ROI-based setting.

title: Distinct spatial organization of human hippocampal perfusion and microvascular pulsatility across age
abstract: Arterial pulsation can modulate neuronal activity through mechanosensitive pathways in mice, but whether vascular pulsatility is similarly related to neural organization in humans remains unclear. Here, using 7T MRI in 35 young and older adults, we mapped cerebral perfusion and microvascular volumetric pulsatility index (mvPI) across the unfolded hippocampus and integrated these measures with histological, electrophysiological, and transcriptomic reference maps. Perfusion and mvPI exhibited distinct spatial organization and age-related differences. In young adults, perfusion preferentially corresponded to parvalbumin-interneuron density and beta/gamma distribution, whereas mvPI was associated with theta-band distribution. A number of associations detected in young adults were not detected in the older adults maps. Spectral simulations showed qualitative similarity to heartbeat-related phase resetting as one possible explanation for the mvPI-theta relationship, while spatial transcriptomics revealed perivascular enrichment of PIEZO2, a candidate mediator of vascular mechanotransduction. Together, these findings establish perfusion and tissue-level pulsatility as distinct dimensions of human hippocampal vascular organization and provide a framework for investigating their relationships with neural dynamics across aging.

title: Diagnostic Accuracy of Fine Needle Aspiration Cytology in Thyroid Diseases: Comparison with Histopathological Findings in Hawassa, Ethiopia
abstract: Introduction: Thyroid diseases are major health problems and among the most common endocrine disorders worldwide, including in Ethiopia. They are characterized by alterations in hormone secretion, enlargement of the thyroid gland, or both. Fine needle aspiration cytology is an important initial screening tool, and histopathologic examination is essential for the definitive diagnosis of thyroid disease. This study aimed to compare the diagnostic accuracy of fine needle aspiration cytology with histopathology in identifying thyroid diseases. Methods: A cross-sectional study was conducted at three health facilities in Hawassa City, Ethiopia, involving 304 patients who underwent both thyroid fine needle aspiration cytology and histopathologic examination of the same site between 30th October 2024 and 29th October 2025. FNAC results were classified using the Bethesda system, with histopathology as the gold standard. Data were entered into Kobo Toolbox, exported to SPSS version 27, and analyzed using cross-tabulation and chi-square (χ²) tests to determine diagnostic accuracy. Result: 304 patient records were included in the study. The fine needle aspiration cytology was determinate/diagnostic in 81.6% of cases. The study revealed the sensitivity and specificity of fine needle aspiration cytology to be 88.2% (CI 77.6-95.1%) and 94.4% (CI 90.6-97.1%), respectively. The false negative and false positive rates in this study were 2.4% and 4.4%, respectively. The positive predictive value was 80.3% (CI 68.7-89.3%), and the negative predictive value was 96.8% (CI 93.8-98.7%). The accuracy of fine needle aspiration cytology in differentiating benign from malignant thyroid lesions was 93.1%. Conclusion: FNAC demonstrated strong agreement with histopathology and remains a reliable, cost-effective first-line diagnostic tool for thyroid disease, particularly in resource-limited settings. Strengthening sample handling, ultrasound guidance, and adherence to Bethesda criteria may further improve diagnostic precision

title: Discrepancies in Interpretation of Japanese Radiology Report Expressions Between Radiologists and Referring Physicians
abstract: Objectives To evaluate discrepancies between radiologists and referring physicians in the interpretation of diagnostic probabilities conveyed by common Japanese expressions used in radiology reports. Materials and Methods Fifteen expressions commonly used to convey diagnostic probabilities in radiology reports were selected by five attending radiologists. An anonymous online survey was distributed to 26 radiologists and 33 referring physicians at a single institution. Participants assigned a diagnostic probability (from 0% to 100% in 10% increments) to each expression. Differences in median probabilities between radiologists and referring physicians were analyzed using the Mann-Whitney U test. Variability in interpretation was assessed using interquartile range (IQR), with IQR [≥] 30% defined as substantial variability. Results All radiologists (26/26) and 97% of referring physicians (32/33) completed the survey. Seven of the 15 expressions showed statistically significant differences in interpretation between radiologists and referring physicians: "c/w" (80% vs. 60%; p = 0.031), the Japanese equivalents of "present" (100% vs. 100%; p = 0.024), "suspect of" (80% vs. 70%; p = 0.007), "possibly" (50% vs. 70%; p < 0.001), "unlikely" (10% vs. 10%; p = 0.022), "cannot be ruled out" (25% vs. 40%; p < 0.001), and "not inconsistent with" (80% vs. 90%; p = 0.008). Substantial variability in interpretation (IQR [≥] 30%) was observed for four expressions: "cannot be ruled out" (IQR, 10%-40%), "s/o" (IQR, 60%-90%), "c/w" (IQR, 50%-90%), and "not inconsistent with" (IQR, 70%-100%). Conclusion This study revealed that nearly half of the Japanese expressions commonly used to convey diagnostic probabilities were interpreted differently by radiologists and referring physicians. These discrepancies highlight the need for a standardized lexicon to improve clarity and consistency in radiology reporting.

title: Beyond Kidney Volume: 3D Mapping of Parenchymal, Cortical and Medullary Thickness with Disease, Anthropometry and Kidney Adiposity
abstract: Introduction: Kidney volume is associated with renal function, but conventional whole-organ measurements may miss regional changes in kidney substructures. We used magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) to test whether kidney substructure volumes and three-dimensional (3D) thickness phenotypes are associated with disease, adiposity, and incident outcomes. Methods: Automated abdominal MRI segmentations from 70,270 UK Biobank participants were used to quantify left and right kidney cortex, medulla, and parenchyma volumes and mesh-based thickness maps. Mass univariate regression generated statistical parametric maps linking regional thickness to anthropometric traits and disease (CKD, type-2 diabetes [T2D], hypertension). Bidirectional causal mediation analyses were performed using kidney substructure volumetric, thickness PCs and kidney adiposity. Longitudinal changes were assessed in 2,610 participants with repeat imaging. Cox proportional hazards models tested the associations between kidney volumes and principal component (PC) scores of thickness and incident CKD, T2D, hypertension, cardiovascular disease (CVD), and mortality. Results: CKD was associated with thinning of the parenchyma and most pronounced in the medulla (87.7% left, 72.8% right), whereas associations in the cortex were mixed. In contrast, T2D and hypertension were predominantly associated with increased thickness, most extensively in the cortex (T2D: 84.39% left, 96.35% right; hypertension: 94.8% left, 99.9% right). Age-disease interactions were associated with reduced thickness across all conditions. Smaller medulla volume and lower cortical thickness mediated the association between CKD and renal sinus fat. Kidney substructure volume was inversely associated with incident CKD across all substructures and both kidney sides (p<0.05), but positively associated with incident hypertension and mortality (p<0.05). Thickness PC scores also predicted outcomes independently of volume, with PC3 in the left cortex (HR 0.91 [0.84-0.98]), reflecting inferior pole/hilar thickness, associated with incident CKD. Conclusions: MRI-derived kidney substructure volumes and 3D thickness maps provide complementary, spatially-resolved markers of kidney morphology, that are mechanistically linked to renal adiposity and future disease risk.

Cox proportional hazards models tested the associations between kidney volumes and principal component (PC) scores of thickness and incident CKD, T2D, hypertension, cardiovascular disease (CVD), and mortality.

Results:

CKD was associated with thinning of the parenchyma and most pronounced in the medulla (87.7% left, 72.8% right), whereas associations in the cortex were mixed. In contrast, T2D and hypertension were predominantly associated with increased thickness, most extensively in the cortex (T2D: 84.39% left, 96.35% right; hypertension: 94.8% left, 99.9% right). Age-disease interactions were associated with reduced thickness across all conditions. Smaller medulla volume and lower cortical thickness mediated the association between CKD and renal sinus fat. Kidney substructure volume was inversely associated with incident CKD across all substructures and both kidney sides (p<0.05), but positively associated with incident hypertension and mortality (p<0.05). Thickness PC scores also predicted outcomes independently of volume, with PC3 in the left cortex (HR 0.91 [0.84-0.98]), reflecting inferior pole/hilar thickness, associated with incident CKD.

Conclusions:

MRI-derived kidney substructure volumes and 3D thickness maps provide complementary, spatially-resolved markers of kidney morphology, that are mechanistically linked to renal adiposity and future disease risk.

title: Cribriform Status at Follow-up Biopsy Is Critical for Predicting Prostate Cancer Active Surveillance Failure in the MRI Era: a Transatlantic Cohort Study
abstract: Purpose: To assess whether follow-up MRI, biopsy status, and timing of cribriform disease detection predict active surveillance (AS) failure in a contemporary transatlantic cohort. Materials and Methods. Retrospective MRI-driven AS cohort of 619 men at two academic centers (UK/USA), 2012-2024. Primary outcome: AS failure (disease-specific mortality, metastasis, grade group [GG] ≥4 progression, or post-treatment biochemical recurrence). Key exposures: final MRI and biopsy status, timing of cribriform ≥GG2 detection. Cumulative incidence was derived; independent predictors used multivariable Fine-Gray models. Results. Over median follow-up of 6.4 years, 39/619 men (6%) experienced AS failure. Cribriform ≥GG2 was detected in 82/619 (13%) on follow-up biopsy versus 24/619 (4%) at baseline, comparably in baseline GG1 (10%) and non-cribriform GG2 (9%), and only in MRI-visible tumors. Three-year AS failure after final biopsy was 31% in men with cribriform ≥GG2 versus 0-2% with stable or non-cribriform disease; 44% of failures had stable MRI. On Fine-Gray analysis, cribriform ≥GG2 was the only independent predictor of AS failure in re-biopsied men (SHR 30; 95% CI 5.2-167; P<0.001); no type of MRI progression category was independently predictive. Among 595 men cribriform-negative at baseline, 6-year AS failure after a second biopsy was 34% if cribriform ≥GG2 was detected versus 7% if still cribriform-negative. Conclusions. Cribriform status at follow-up biopsy independently predicts AS failure, whereas MRI progression does not. The three-fold higher cribriform prevalence at follow-up likely reflects baseline sampling error. Because newly detected cribriform tumours were exclusively MRI-visible, early repeat biopsy of patients with MRI-visible disease may considerably improve risk stratification.

title: Proximal sesamoid bone fatigue in Thoroughbred racehorses is associated with palmar osteochondral disease in the adjacent third metacarpal bone condyle
abstract: Abstract Background: Proximal sesamoid bone (PSB) stress fracture is a common catastrophic injury in racing Thoroughbreds that is associated with bone sclerosis and development of focal osteolysis. Standing computed tomography (sCT) enables sensitive identification of these structural changes and associations with other more common fetlock fatigue injury such as palmar/plantar osteochondral disease lesions affecting the condyles of the third metacarpal/metatarsal (MC3/MT3). Objective: To gain insight into the PSB stress fracture mechanism, we examined associations between fatigue injury prevalence in the three major metacarpophalangeal (MCP) sites: PSB, parasagittal grooves (PSG), and third metacarpal bone MC3 condyles. Study design: Retrospective clinical study. Methods: We studied 22 catastrophically injured Thoroughbred racehorses. Thoracic limbs were examined using computed tomography (CT) (n=29). Subjective CT assessment classified 58 PSBs as 32 control and 26 case PSBs with bone fatigue (transverse fracture, focal osteolysis, or severe sclerosis). Opposing joint surfaces were also studied. PSB bone mineral density (BMD) was estimated. Results: Prevalence of fatigue injury in the PSB, condyle, and PSG was 44.8% (n=26), 43.1% (n=25), and 17.2% (n=10), respectively. For MC3 condyles with POD, 88.0% had fatigue injury in the corresponding PSB (OR = 53.2). Prevalence of PSB fatigue injury was 20.0% when there was PSG fatigue injury. The odds of a PSB having fatigue injury when the opposing MC3 PSG had signs of fatigue injury was 0.25. PSBs with opposing MC3 condyles containing a POD lesion had significantly increased BMD compared with opposing control condyles. BMD was significantly increased in PSBs with structural change associated with cyclic fatigue. Conclusions: Development of PSB fatigue and adaptive PSB sclerosis is associated with POD. Stress fractures in Thoroughbreds commonly affect the MCP joint. Condylar fractures occur from PSG or POD fatigue injury. PSB fractures are also common. Our findings suggest detailed clinical assessment of PSB structural change in racing Thoroughbreds diagnosed with POD is merited as part of routine injury prevention screening.

title: Structural damage of the cervical spinal cord within and beyond the maximal compression area in mucopolysaccharidosis types I and VI
abstract: Background: Cervical spinal cord (CSC) compression and myelopathy are frequent, severe complications in mucopolysaccharidosis (MPS) types I and VI. Early detection is critical to prevent irreversible neurological deficits and preserve quality of life. This prospective study aimed to identify quantitative neuroimaging biomarkers of structural CSC damage and myelopathy in MPS I and VI. Methods: Structural and diffusion magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) of the CSC was analyzed in 17 MPS I patients, 3 MPS VI patients (19{+/-}7 years), and 19 case-matched healthy controls (20{+/-}7 years). CSC macrostructure (cross-sectional area, diameters) and microstructure (fractional anisotropy [FA], radial [RD], mean, axial diffusivities) were evaluated within and beyond the maximal compression areas. Results: MPS patients demonstrated reduced CSC cross-sectional area and anterior-posterior diameter at upper cervical levels, alongside widespread microstructural alterations (lower FA, higher RD) throughout the CSC versus controls (pFDR<0.05). Restricted foramen magnum space was associated with microstructural damage at lower cervical levels without overt macrostructural compression. Morphological and microstructural metrics were sensitive to CSC compression and myelopathy severity (pFDR<0.05). Lower CSC integrity correlated with more advanced growth retardation (p<0.001). Among patients receiving hematopoietic stem cell transplantation, earlier treatment correlated with preserved upper CSC morphology (p<0.05). Distinct neuroimaging phenotypes were observed across MPS genotypes (pFDR<0.05). Conclusions: CSC MRI provides candidate neuroimaging biomarkers for early detection and characterization of myelopathy in MPS I and VI. Structural damage extends beyond primary maximal compression areas, highlighting these markers for clinical monitoring and future therapeutic trials.

title: Privacy-Preserving Personalized Federated Learning (PPP-FL) for Medical Imaging
abstract: Federated learning (FL) is a distributed machine learning paradigm that reduces transmission costs, mitigates cross-border data sharing restrictions, and enhances privacy by keeping raw data on local devices. Clients in FL systems train local models and share only updates, which are aggregated by a central server. While this setup limits direct data exposure, FL remains vulnerable to privacy attacks. Existing attack and defense strategies have largely been developed for centralized systems, and adapting them to FL introduces new challenges due to its unique architecture and training workflow. In this work, we first propose a model inversion attack on FL systems using Deep Convolutional Generative Adversarial Networks (DCGANs) in the context of large-scale medical imaging. Our method operates under realistic assumptions about the attacker's knowledge and capabilities. We then examine the effect of client-side differential privacy (DP) in mitigating privacy leakage and incorporate personalized FL to improve model performance under DP settings. Experiments on the Brain MRI ND-5 dataset show that DCGAN-based attacks can reconstruct semantically meaningful synthetic images, revealing significant risks to the privacy of training data. Applying DP reduces attack success but introduces an accuracy trade-off, which is further overcome by personalized FL at each client side. We also evaluate how different aggregation algorithms affect both attack vulnerability and defense effectiveness, underscoring the critical role of aggregation strategies. The proposed attack-and-defense framework is model-agnostic and applicable to a wide range of FL-based systems.

title: DART: Scaling a Shape Representation Across Anatomical Classes and Imaging Modalities
abstract: Current state-of-the-art segmentation models still produce anatomically implausible shapes, such as broken vessels and fragmented glands, on the structures that are hardest to segment. Learned shape representations capture what structures look like and can help correct these errors, but most cover a fixed set of anatomical classes. Extending this coverage across classes and imaging modalities is costly because it often requires new voxel-level annotations. We propose Diffusion for Anatomical Reshaping with Text (DART), which learns a shared shape representation from segmentation probabilities. It uses anatomical descriptions to correct these probabilities without receiving medical images. Across 13 public benchmarks, absolute Dice gains reach 31% for individual gallbladder cases in CT and 10% for individual prostate cases in MRI. Using existing segmentation predictions, we scale a single shape representation from 50 to 377 anatomical classes without new voxel-level annotations for correction training. The shared representation also corrects four lesion classes absent from training and transfers from CT to MRI without retraining. Corrected labels also improve segmentation models, raising one model's Dice from 57.1% to 67.5%. The same pipeline supports annotations for 45,000 CT scans. These results suggest that sharing shape information within and across classes can reduce the need for new voxel-level annotations when extending segmentation to more anatomical classes and imaging modalities. The model is available at https://huggingface.co/Koushik45/DART-Seg

title: Beyond the Evidence Boundary: Behavioral Mirage Under Progressive Degradation in Medical VLMs
abstract: VLMs for medical image interpretation are typically evaluated on clean inputs, despite the progressive evidence loss that can occur in high stakes clinical settings. Existing robustness studies show that performance can degrade while confidence remains high, but do not establish when a previously reliable model-case pair ceases to behave reliably. We introduce a baseline-anchored framework that traces baseline-correct cases through progressive image degradation to identify an empirical evidence boundary, and define mirage as continued commitment at this boundary, regardless of correctness. Across three VLMs on three medical datasets, only MedGemma provides a sufficiently large baseline-correct pool for trajectory analysis. On VQA-RAD, the only dataset in which the question text varies, language-only answerability is associated with baseline correctness (AUROC 0.677) and with commitment at the boundary (AUROC 0.653 to 0.670). MedGemma's post-boundary behavior is heterogeneous, including direct mirage, correct recovery, mirage dissolution, consistent abstention, and oscillation, with mirage rates of 16.0 to 100.0% across dataset-modality pairs. Despite this behavioral heterogeneity, residual-stream probes decode commit-versus-abstain behavior at the boundary with AUROC of 0.895 to 0.994 under nested cross-validation. These results show that progressive evidence loss can produce persistent commitment that output entropy and abstention behavior do not consistently reflect, motivating boundary-aware evaluation, option-order controls, and improved abstention mechanisms for reliable medical foundation models operating under partial observation.

title: AdaptMIL: Domain Adaptation for Multiple Instance Learning in Digital Pathology
abstract: Pathology foundation models (PFMs) support a wide range of histopathology tasks on whole-slide images through multiple instance learning (MIL). Despite recent progress, these models remain sensitive to cross-hospital distribution shifts: performance often degrades when a task head (e.g., classification) is trained on data from one hospital and then used on data from another hospital. To address this challenge, we propose AdaptMIL, a training strategy for integrating domain adaptation into MIL training. AdaptMIL is motivated by our finding that directly applying domain adaptation objectives during MIL training can interfere with MIL aggregation learning, often resulting in performance degradation over standard training. AdaptMIL resolves this by decoupling representation-level domain alignment learning from MIL aggregation learning through a two-stage training procedure. We show that AdaptMIL improves cross-hospital performance and outperforms alternative adaptation methods across experiments spanning multiple WSI datasets, tasks, PFMs, MIL architectures, and domain adaptation objectives. AdaptMIL's code will be released upon publication.

title: LatticeRank: Spacing-Ranked Consistency for Native-Grid 3D Medical Image Segmentation
abstract: Variable voxel spacing changes more than image resolution: it alters the discrete sampling lattice, tensor geometry, and anatomical evidence available to a 3D segmentation network. While conventional pipelines restore images to a canonical grid, direct-grid deployment requires the model itself to tolerate these changes. We observe that candidate grids are not exchangeable views -- a coarse grid removes more structural information than a mildly resampled one -- yet standard consistency objectives assign them equal influence. We therefore propose LatticeRank, a training-only framework that aligns candidate posteriors in physical space and allocates consistency supervision by voxel-spacing order: among endpoint-matched candidates, the auxiliary loss concentrates on the coarsest requested grid, while inference retains a single network forward with no candidate branch or ensemble. On MSD Task04, LatticeRank improves coarse-grid Extra Dice over mean consistency by 0.03436 across five seeds while meeting the prespecified reference-grid noninferiority criterion. A controlled ladder shows that grid exposure provides the largest recovery, posterior consistency adds a second gain, and spacing-ranked allocation yields the strongest direct-grid result; requested spacing thus provides a simple, model-independent ordering signal for direct-grid consistency learning.

title: Reliability-Guided Vision-Language Decoding with Text-Aware Skip Refinement for Medical Image Segmentation
abstract: Medical image segmentation remains challenging when targets exhibit limited visual distinction, irregular structure, or substantial variation across imaging modalities. Medical text can reduce this ambiguity, but indiscriminate fusion may introduce unreliable guidance. We present RELiF, a vision--language framework that integrates text through reliability-guided decoding. Its Reliability-guided Fusion Gate (RFG) adaptively controls cross-modal updates, while the Text-guided Skip Refinement Adapter (TSRA) refines high-resolution features using text guidance. RELiF is evaluated on radiographic, CT, and endoscopic segmentation tasks, where it shows competitive performance across diverse imaging characteristics and target appearances. Additional analyses examine efficiency and stability. The complementary uncertainty representation derived from the reliability response also shows an association with prediction difficulty, with higher uncertainty values occurring more frequently in pixels associated with segmentation errors. Code: https://github.com/SeivanTalaie/RELiF.

title: CAPS: Clinically-Verifiable Anatomy-Prioritized Synthesis for Missing MRI Imputation in Brain Tumor Segmentation
abstract: Multi-parametric MRI is the gold standard for neuro-oncology, yet acquiring complete 4-modality protocols may be unfeasible in real-world clinical practice. When handling missing modalities, existing automated systems force a critical compromise: robust segmenters operate as uninterpretable "black boxes" that bypass image generation, while standard synthesis models often produce blurry reconstructions lacking diagnostic reliability. To address this issue, we propose CAPS, a Clinically-Verifiable Anatomy-Prioritized Synthesis framework that reconciles computational precision with clinical transparency. Our multi-modal generative architecture is driven by a hybrid objective function (L_1 + L_AFP + L_DualDice) that explicitly enforces the preservation of deep anatomical features and strict topological boundaries, rather than relying solely on pixel-wise optimization. Evaluated comprehensively on the BraTS Adult Glioma dataset, the framework achieves superior synthesis fidelity across intensity-based metrics, and demonstrates robust downstream segmentation performance (82.38% mean Dice), successfully restoring verifiable visual context. Furthermore, the framework exhibits exceptional zero-shot cross-domain generalization, maintaining high structural fidelity across completely unseen Meningioma, Pediatric, and Sub-Saharan African cohorts without domain-specific adaptation. Finally, a blinded radiological assessment confirms that our anatomy-aware approach significantly enhances both perceived image quality and clinical utility, providing clinicians with the reliable visual evidence required to trust downstream automated workflows.

title: Convergent Performance, Divergent Mechanisms in LoRA-Adapted Vision Foundation Models for Brain MRI
abstract: Adapting Vision Foundation Models (VFMs) to medical imaging via LoRA has become standard practice, yet model selection is guided almost entirely by downstream task metrics, treating backbones with similar performance as interchangeable. We investigate whether equal performance implies equal internal representational shift. We analyse four ViT-B/16 backbones, DINOv3, SigLIP2, MerMED-FM, and BiomedCLIP, pre-trained with different objectives (self-distillation vs. contrastive vision-language) and on different data domains (natural vs. medical images). We adapt each to brain tumour segmentation and evaluate on six datasets covering both segmentation and Alzheimer's disease classification. Using attention divergence, weight-change analysis, and activation patching, we find that the four models converge to similar segmentation performance (mean Dice 78-81%) through markedly different internal dynamics, yet diverge in cross-task transfer: segmentation adaptation improves Alzheimer's disease classification for DINOv3 but degrades it for the other three backbones. We reveal a dissociation between modification magnitude and causal importance: the most heavily modified layers are not the causally relevant ones, with early-to-mid layers identified as sufficient for segmentation recovery. Restricting LoRA to these layers matches or approaches full-layer segmentation while reducing classification degradation in the three affected backbones, providing a mechanistically grounded strategy that is more parameter-efficient and more robust than standard full-layer adaptation.

We reveal a dissociation between modification magnitude and causal importance: the most heavily modified layers are not the causally relevant ones, with early-to-mid layers identified as sufficient for segmentation recovery. Restricting LoRA to these layers matches or approaches full-layer segmentation while reducing classification degradation in the three affected backbones, providing a mechanistically grounded strategy that is more parameter-efficient and more robust than standard full-layer adaptation.

title: CPVB-RG: Cross-Prior Visual Bridging for Prior-Aware Chest X-Ray Report Generation
abstract: Radiologists interpret follow-up chest X-rays by comparing current and prior examinations to identify new, resolved or progressing findings. Most report generation systems either omit this longitudinal context or fuse prior features without distinguishing interval changes from anatomy that remains stable over time. We propose CPVB-RG, a prior-aware framework that combines current and prior radiographs with available clinical text. Its Cross-Prior Visual Bridge (CPVB) contains Progression-Guided Focus Attention (PGFA) and two Cross-Attention units. PGFA is designed to contrast progression-difference attention with shared-spatial attention, aiming to reduce invariant responses whilst retaining coarse spatial correspondence between examinations. The Cross-Attention units then connect the resulting longitudinal visual evidence with clinical semantics. CPVB-RG is trained in two stages, using prior-guided image-text alignment followed by autoregressive report generation with a lightweight language decoder. Experiments on MIMIC-CXR and IU X-Ray show consistent improvements across language and clinical metrics. On MIMIC-CXR, CPVB-RG achieves 0.2847 F1RadGraph and 0.6692 VLScore, with statistically significant gains over the closest decoder-matched prior-aware baseline. These results support the effectiveness of the proposed difference-aware and spatially guided fusion design for prior-aware chest X-ray report generation.

title: AGGR-Mamba: Mamba-based Network with Attention-Guided Gated Residual Refinement for Undersampled MRI Reconstruction
abstract: Undersampled magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) reconstruction aims to recover high-quality images from partially acquired k-space data, thereby reducing scan time. However, missing frequency-domain measurements often lead to residual aliasing artifacts, blurred edges, and loss of local structural details. In this paper, we propose AGGR-Mamba, a lightweight output-stage residual refinement method built upon a Mamba backbone for undersampled brain MRI reconstruction. The Mamba backbone first produces an initial reconstruction, and the proposed refinement modules then correct the remaining local errors and high-frequency artifacts in a controlled residual manner. Specifically, an Attention Refine Head is introduced to recalibrate local anatomical structures, edge textures, and residual-error regions through channel and spatial attention. In addition, a GDFN-style gated residual refinement branch is designed to selectively preserve informative residual features while suppressing redundant or unstable responses. By combining attention-based recalibration with gated residual selection, AGGR-Mamba improves local structure recovery without substantially disturbing the backbone reconstruction. Experiments are conducted on the IXI brain MRI dataset with T1- and T2-weighted images under acceleration factors of R=4 and R=8. The results show that AGGR-Mamba achieves competitive PSNR and SSIM performance across different reconstruction settings, demonstrating the effectiveness of the proposed output-stage refinement strategy.

title: A Multi-Agent Framework for Automated Machine Learning with Evidence-based Planning for Medical Image Analysis
abstract: Deep learning has become the default tool for medical image analysis, driven by the open-source movement. However, achieving the best performance on a given task remains difficult, with architecture selection and hyperparameter optimization (HPO) still considered "more of an art than a science". Automated machine learning (AutoML) automates parts of model training, yet helps little in medical imaging: general-purpose approaches lack medical architectures and preprocessing, and medical-focused ones demand engineering expertise and remain confined to narrow tasks such as 3D segmentation. We introduce MedicalMLOmni, a multi-agent AutoML framework that automates model training for diverse single- and multi-modal medical tasks through a natural language interface. Specifically, MedicalMLOmni performs evidence-based planning by retrieving published results to guide model selection and configuration, and employs parallel HPO where multiple agents explore adjustment strategies concurrently. MedicalMLOmni achieves the best score on 19 of 20 benchmarks; PMC-VQA is the exception, where a vision-language model with broader pre-training leads. Backbone-matched controls attribute the gains to the framework, not the backbone. By removing coding requirements, MedicalMLOmni lowers the barrier for domain experts with rich datasets but limited engineering expertise.

title: Brain2Vec: A Self-Supervised 3D Foundation Model for Structural Brain MRI
abstract: Deep learning models have become essential tools in medical imaging, yet training them end-to-end for diverse tasks remains challenging due to limited labeled data and computational constraints. To address this, we introduce Brain2Vec, a foundation model pre-trained on 74,425 T1-weighted Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) scans pooled from multiple studies. Brain2Vec can serve both as a weight initialization backbone for fine-tuning downstream tasks and as a standalone feature extractor. We evaluated Brain2Vec in three tasks: downstream predictive performance, convergence speed, and embedding quality. Using Brain2Vec's pretrained weights as initialization and fine-tuning on labeled data for a brain age prediction task, results demonstrate improved final accuracy and faster convergence compared to random initialization. Additionally, its frozen embeddings outperform anatomically defined volumetric features on four of five downstream classification tasks and perform competitively with a state-of-the-art foundation model pre-trained on substantially more data. Lastly, we show that Brain2Vec encodes information primarily from a spatially localized and neuroanatomically meaningful set of brain regions, and that manipulating a subset of latent features produces monotonic, region-specific effects on the reconstructed anatomy. Brain2Vec code and trained models are available as an open-source package on https://github.com/CBICA/Brain2Vec. Users can apply Brain2Vec locally by installing the package, or directly through the NiChart cloud platform https://cloud.neuroimagingchart.com, where Brain2Vec features can be derived without requiring local installation or specialized infrastructure.

title: Improved three component IVIM fitting using physics-informed neural network with multimodal spatial prior
abstract: Purpose: To mitigate parameter degeneracy and improve robustness of IVIM fitting, a multimodal physics-informed neural network was developed to leverage anatomical information through the combined use of cross attention, selective spatial gating, and anatomy-weighted spatial prior. Methods: T1w and FLAIR anatomical images were co-registered to IVIM signal in native space and segmented by tissue type. The proposed Physics-Anchored Cross-attention Embedding network (PACE) encoded IVIM signals and their anatomical features in parallel branches, then integrated them via cross attention and spatial gating. An anatomy-weighted spatial prior further constrained signal reconstruction using anatomically similar neighboring voxels. PACE and its prior-guided variant were compared with two baseline deep neural networks (DNN and IVIM3C), least squares, non-negative least squares, and maximum a posteriori fitting models. All models were evaluated on signal and parameter reconstruction accuracy and lesion contrast fidelity using data generated from subjects drawn from the University of Rochester COVID cohort. Results: PACE variants demonstrated lower RMSE for all IVIM parameters except for Dmv. The anatomy-weighted spatial prior further reduced RMSE across all five parameters relative to the default PACE, with modest reductions in lesion contrast accuracy for fmv and fint. For in-vivo evaluation, PACE with spatial prior also showed the best signal reconstruction across all noise levels while maintaining good to excellent ICC. Conclusion: Multimodal anatomical information improved IVIM fitting accuracy and robustness, with selective spatial integration via cross attention, gating, and anatomy-weighted spatial prior. Keywords: intravoxel incoherent motion, physics-informed deep learning, diffusion MRI, multimodality fusion, attention mechanism

title: MedBOE: Optimization-Based Estimation of Complete Patient Body Models from Whole-Body Medical Imaging
abstract: True whole-body medical imaging captures a patient from head to toe and provides comprehensive anatomical and/or functional information. This coverage enables reconstruction of the external body surface, yielding patient body models. However, scanner geometry (e.g., bore diameter), patient characteristics, and positioning can leave body regions missing (e.g., lateral arms/torso, hands, forearms, elbows), producing incomplete patient body models. Such incompleteness limits downstream medical analyses, including derivation of body-habitus metrics (BHMs), such as body volume and surface area, for injected radiotracer activity regimens, cardiometabolic risk assessment, and computational anatomical modeling for medical imaging simulation and radiation dosimetry. We present the Medical Body model Optimization-based Estimator (MedBOE), an automated, training-free framework for estimating complete patient body models from whole-body images with missing body regions. Our innovation is to leverage the Skinned Multi-Person Linear (SMPL) template, a parametric body mesh representing a broad range of body shapes and poses, in medical imaging. MedBOE aligns the SMPL template to the incomplete patient body models via attribute-guided optimization and estimates missing body regions through geometrically and volumetrically constrained deformation. We evaluated MedBOE using two public datasets: AutoPET (91 whole-body PET-CT images) and Human Implicit Tissues (HIT; 40 whole-body segmentations from MRI images). MedBOE achieved the best overall volumetric and geometric performance among evaluated methods. BHMs derived from MedBOE were within 2% error, suggesting low percentage errors for downstream analyses. MedBOE offers an automated, training-free method for estimating complete patient body models from whole-body images with missing body regions.

title: Tumour Antigen-Specific Antibody Signatures as Diagnostic Biomarkers for Melanoma.
abstract: Early detection of melanoma remains challenging, and minimally invasive diagnostic tools are needed to complement imaging and histopathology. Circulating tumour antigen-specific antibodies (Abs) are promising biomarkers, but their diagnostic value across melanoma stages is not fully established. Circulating IgG and IgM Abs were profiled in plasma from two independent melanoma cohorts, early-stage (n = 65) and advanced-stage (n = 77), alongside healthy controls (n = 86) and individuals with prior cancer in remission (n = 37). A protein microarray containing 263 tumour antigens, predominantly cancer-testis (CT) antigens, was used to measure plasma antibody (Ab) reactivity. Univariate and multivariate ROC analyses identified candidate diagnostic biomarker signatures. Early-stage melanoma was best distinguished by an IgM signature comprising AURKA, BAGE3, BAGE4, CDK7, CEP290, MYBL2, PIAS2, RAD51 and SPANXB1 (AUC = 0.939). An IgG signature including ANKRD45, BCL2L14, CDK2, MAGEA4v3, MAPK3 and RBM46 achieved AUC = 0.827. Advanced-stage melanoma exhibited broader Ab repertoires, including an IgG signature (CTAG1A, DKKL1, PIWIL2, SPANXN1, TSGA10, TSPY1; AUC = 0.865) and an IgM signature (CPXCR1, CSAG2, FMR1NB, FOXR2, LIPI, MAGEA5, TSGA10; AUC = 0.889). Individuals in cancer remission displayed persistent Ab signatures distinct from early melanoma and healthy controls. Overlap between IgG and IgM repertoires was minimal, highlighting complementary discriminatory value. Circulating IgG and IgM Abs against tumour antigens reveal stage-specific signatures that distinguish melanoma from healthy individuals and those in cancer remission, identifying candidate discovery-stage diagnostic biomarker signatures warranting independent validation in larger prospective cohorts to determine clinical utility.

title: Contrast-Enhanced Ultrasound in the Diagnosis of Parotid Gland Castleman Disease in a Child.
abstract: Castleman disease is a rare lymphoproliferative disorder that infrequently involves the parotid gland. We report a 16-year-old girl with a 3-year history of slowly progressive, painless right cheek swelling. CT and MRI showed an avidly enhancing, markedly T2-hyperintense parotid lesion, suggesting a vascular malformation; fine-needle aspiration yielded reactive lymphoid tissue. Contrast-enhanced ultrasound (CEUS) demonstrated rapid, intense, homogeneous enhancement, confirming a hypervascular solid mass rather than a vascular malformation and raising suspicion for Castleman disease. Superficial parotidectomy confirmed unicentric hyaline-vascular Castleman disease. CEUS aided differentiation of a hypervascular solid lesion from a vascular malformation and narrowed the differential.

title: Sonographic Diagnosis and Anatomic Mapping of a Radial Artery Pseudoaneurysm Following Transradial Cardiac Catheterization.
abstract: Radial artery pseudoaneurysm is a rare complication of transradial catheterization. We report a 74-year-old woman on rivaroxaban who developed a pulsatile distal forearm mass 1 day after transradial cardiac catheterization. High-frequency ultrasound showed a rounded extra-arterial lesion (7.6 × 8.9 × 7.0 mm) not involving all wall layers, with thrombus, a discrete communicating neck, turbulent bidirectional "yin-yang" color Doppler, and preserved distal flow. Anatomic mapping showed the lesion abutting adjacent tendons and the palmar cutaneous branch of the median nerve. Surgical excision and microscopic repair succeeded. Sonographic characterization provided anatomic detail that, with clinical and surgical assessment, informed individualized management.
