title: Is the use of Porous Threaded Titanium Implants Associated with Lower Rates of Implant Migration in Elderly Pelvic Ring Injuries?
abstract: Objectives To determine if porous threaded titanium implant (PTTI) screws placed in the posterior pelvic ring as iliosacral (IS) or transiliac-transsacral (transsacral) were associated with implant positional changes, alterations in postoperative weightbearing restrictions, or the necessity of revision surgery in operatively managed geriatric pelvic ring injuries, compared to standard stainless steel screws. Methods Design Retrospective cohort study. Setting Academic Level I trauma center. Patient selection criteria Patients with operatively managed pelvic ring injuries (AO/OTA61) from January 2017 to June 2025, aged ≥65 years with a minimum of 6-months of radiographic and clinical follow-up were included.Outcome Measures and Comparisons: The primary study outcome was the incidence of postoperative pelvic ring implant positional changes, ≥2mm from immediate postoperative radiographs compared among patients treated with PTTI versus standard stainless steel screws for IS and transsacral fixation. Secondary outcomes included subsequent revision surgery or alterations in postoperative weightbearing restrictions related to implant positional changes. A multivariable logistic regression was used to determine associations of demographic, injury, and treatment variables with implant positional changes, the necessity for revision surgery, or negative changes in postoperative weightbearing restrictions. Results 271 patients were included; 215 (79.3%) were managed with standard screws, while PTTIs were used in 56 (20.7%). The standard screw cohort had a median follow-up of 8.9 months (interquartile range 6.2-11.3 months), while the PTTI cohort had a median follow-up of 9.1 months (interquartile range 6.3-10.9 months). Compared with the standard screw cohort, the PTTI cohort had a higher proportion of female sex (57.2% versus 73.2%, respectively; p=0.029) and a higher average age (74.0 years versus 78.6 years, respectively; p<0.001).Radiographic migration ≥2mm for posterior implants was observed in 18.1% of patients in the standard implant cohort versus 0.0% in the PTTI cohort (p<0.001). Implant migration >1cm was observed in 3.7% of patients in the standard implant cohort versus 0.0% in the PTTI group (p=0.231). The implant positional changes resulted in negative weightbearing restriction changes in 9 of 215 (4.2%) patients in the standard implant cohort compared with 0 of 56 in the PTTI cohort (p=0.120). Of the patients with standard implants, 9 (4.2%) underwent revision for posterior implant loosening, compared with 0 (0.0%) in the PTTI cohort.On multivariate analysis, posterior implant positional changes were associated with a protective effect from PTTI and anterior ring fixation (OR 0.1, 95% CI 0.0-0.7, p=0.023 and OR 0.2, 95% CI 0.1-0.4, p<0.001, respectively). The necessity for revision surgery or negative change in postoperative weightbearing restrictions was not significantly associated with PTTI use (OR 0.3, 95% CI 0.1-1.3, p=0.106). Conclusions In geriatric pelvic ring injuries, PTTIs had no migration after placement and were associated with a lower incidence of any implant positional change and posterior implant positional changes. Level of evidence Prognostic Level III.

title: Artificial intelligence in personalized internal dosimetry for radiopharmaceutical therapy: a narrative mini-review.
abstract: Personalized internal radiation dosimetry supports individualized radiopharmaceutical therapy but remains difficult to implement because workflows require repeated quantitative imaging, segmentation, registration, kinetic modeling, and absorbed-dose calculation. This mini-review summarizes current evidence on artificial intelligence across the personalized dosimetry workflow and considers clinical readiness. A narrative PubMed search was completed in early 2026 and covered peer-reviewed studies published from 2015 to early 2026. Studies addressing artificial intelligence, machine learning, or deep learning in quantitative image reconstruction, segmentation, registration, time-activity curve estimation, absorbed-dose calculation, or clinical decision support were considered. Studies reporting quantitative performance or validation results were prioritized. Deep learning reduced yttrium-90 single-photon emission computed tomography reconstruction error from 149.5% ± 31.2% to 9.2% ± 1.7%; lesion dose-rate error was 8.6% ± 5.7% in virtual-patient testing. Learning-based registration reduced computation time from about 50 s to under 6 s. Single-time-point approaches can simplify imaging, and recent machine learning work has explored prediction of organ effective half-life. Automated segmentation methods show improving reproducibility, whereas evidence for artificial intelligence-based clinical decision support remains mainly retrospective and single-center. Artificial intelligence applications in reconstruction and segmentation appear closer to clinical readiness, while decision-support applications still require prospective, multicenter validation.

title: Plasma Phosphorylated Tau 217 Reshapes Diagnostic Classification in a Real-World Memory Clinic Cohort.
abstract: Background Plasma phosphorylated tau-217 (ptau217) accurately identifies Alzheimer disease (AD), but its impact on real-world clinical diagnosis remains unclear. We evaluated the effect of plasma ptau217 on diagnostic reclassification in a memory disorders clinic. Methods We retrospectively reviewed 100 patients evaluated for memory impairment. Initial clinical diagnoses were established based on clinical evaluation, neuropsychological testing, and brain MRI without plasma biomarker results. Follow-up diagnoses were assigned after the availability of plasma ptau217 results. Diagnostic reclassification was assessed using binary (ptau217 > 0.18) and higher threshold (ptau217 > 0.325) classification schemes. McNemar tests evaluated reclassification patterns, with subgroup analyses by apolipoprotein E (APOE) ε4 carrier status. Results Diagnosis reclassification occurred in 37.8% and 46.9% of patients using the lower and higher threshold, respectively (both P<0.001). With the higher threshold (ptau217 > 0.325), reclassification among APOE ε4 carriers was balanced (42% from AD to non-AD vs. 43% from non-AD to AD, P=0.096). In contrast, APOE ε4 noncarriers showed significantly greater reclassification from AD to non-AD than from non-AD to AD (66% vs.14%, P<0.001). Conclusions Plasma ptau217 meaningfully influences diagnostic decisions in memory clinic practice and may be particularly valuable for refining diagnoses among APOE ε4 noncarriers.

Initial clinical diagnoses were established based on clinical evaluation, neuropsychological testing, and brain MRI without plasma biomarker results. Follow-up diagnoses were assigned after the availability of plasma ptau217 results. Diagnostic reclassification was assessed using binary (ptau217 > 0.18) and higher threshold (ptau217 > 0.325) classification schemes. McNemar tests evaluated reclassification patterns, with subgroup analyses by apolipoprotein E (APOE) ε4 carrier status.

Diagnosis reclassification occurred in 37.8% and 46.9% of patients using the lower and higher threshold, respectively (both P<0.001). With the higher threshold (ptau217 > 0.325), reclassification among APOE ε4 carriers was balanced (42% from AD to non-AD vs. 43% from non-AD to AD, P=0.096). In contrast, APOE ε4 noncarriers showed significantly greater reclassification from AD to non-AD than from non-AD to AD (66% vs.14%, P<0.001).

Conclusions

Plasma ptau217 meaningfully influences diagnostic decisions in memory clinic practice and may be particularly valuable for refining diagnoses among APOE ε4 noncarriers.

title: Novel therapies for glioblastoma.
abstract: Purpose of review Glioblastoma is the most aggressive and treatment-resistant primary brain tumor in adults. Given its clinical severity and biological complexity, research efforts are focused on understanding and targeting intratumoral heterogeneity, adaptive resistance, drug delivery barriers, and the immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment. This review highlights emerging therapeutic approaches for the treatment of glioblastoma including advances in radiation planning, molecularly targeted therapy, immunotherapy, blood-brain barrier modulation, and neuronal signaling. Recent findings Radiation therapy remains a cornerstone of glioblastoma treatment, and advances in image-guided planning are being developed to refine treatment margins and improve tolerability without compromising efficacy. Blood-brain barrier permeability is being improved through device-assisted approaches, including focused ultrasound in combination with systemic therapies. Molecularly targeted and immunotherapeutic approaches continue to be evaluated, increasingly with biomarker-informed strategies to optimize patient selection. In parallel, drug repurposing, neuronal modulation, and metabolic interventions have shown promising preclinical and retrospective signals and are moving towards prospective studies. Interventions to improve quality of life are also underway with early palliative care showing significant impact for patients with glioblastoma. Summary As the field moves towards tailored and precision-guided approaches, combination strategies remain central to addressing the multiple mechanisms by which glioblastoma evades treatment.

title: Artificial Intelligence in Paediatric Dentistry: A Scoping Review.
abstract: This review scoped artificial intelligence (AI) in paediatric dentistry to summarize current applications and limitations. A comprehensive literature search was completed across PubMed, Google Scholar, Scopus, Embase, IEEE Xplore, and medRxiv/aArXiv. The preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses Extension for Scoping Reviews (PRISMA-ScR) checklist was used for reporting the present study. Studies concerning paediatric dentistry and utilizing AI, machine learning (ML) or large language models (LLMs) were included. Two independent reviewers screened and three extracted data on AI methodologies, performance metrics, and clinical applications. Fifty-nine studies were included. Computer vision studies (n = 32) most often used panoramic radiographs (n = 14), mainly for tooth detection, numbering and segmentation (n = 10) and caries detection (n = 9). Non-imaging ML studies (n = 18) primarily used clinical variables and questionnaire data (n = 8) or salivary/biological samples (n = 10). Accuracy ranged from 50% to 100%, with sensitivity reaching 100% in biomarker-based studies. LLM accuracy varied widely (33%-96%). Computer vision and non-imaging ML show promise for paediatric dentistry, particularly in the detection of dental structures and diseases, as well as risk stratification. Variable LLM performance underscores the need for standardized evaluation before clinical integration. CLINICAL RELEVANCE: AI-based tools may support paediatric dentists by improving tooth detection, dental structure assessment, caries detection, disease prediction and risk stratification. Computer vision and non-imaging machine learning approaches appear to have potential, but their clinical value depends on robust external validation, transparent reporting and integration into paediatric dental workflows. Given their variable performance, AI tools should be used only as adjunctive tools or a second reviewer.

title: An artificial intelligence model combining MRI and ultrasound images (MRUSuNet) for prostate cancer detection outperforms radiologist MRI interpretation.
abstract: Objectives To develop the magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)-UltraSound UNet (MRUSuNet), a model that uses both MRI and transrectal ultrasonography (TRUS) as input to detect and localise the three-dimensional spatial volume of clinically significant prostate cancer on TRUS images to allow better visualisation of cancer in the TRUS space. Patients and methods Pre-biopsy MRI is increasingly used to target suspicious prostate lesions. The lesions identified by radiologists are mapped onto TRUS images to enable real-time targeting during the biopsy. Yet, the misalignment of MRI and TRUS results in sampling errors, and in some cases even missing the clinically significant cancers. This study included two MRI-TRUS fusion biopsy cohorts (3000 patients) for model development, and one radical prostatectomy cohort (110 patients) used for independent validation and for the comparison with radiologist interpretation. A total of 1700 independent cases were reserved to compare the MRUSuNet with single-modality MRI-only and TRUS-only models. Sensitivity and lesion-level Dice similarity scores were computed using targeted biopsy pathology as the reference standard in the biopsy cohorts and whole-mount prostatectomy pathology in the radical prostatectomy cohort. Result The MRUSuNet achieved significantly superior sensitivity (0.80) and lesion Dice score (0.42) across all test cohorts compared to the MRI-only model (sensitivity: 0.73, P = 0.033; Dice score: 0.30, P < 0.001) and the TRUS-only model (sensitivity: 0.49, P < 0.001; Dice score: 0.27, P < 0.001). Compared to radiologists in the prostatectomy cohort, the MRUSuNet showed significantly higher specificity (0.88 vs 0.78; P = 0.004) and lesion Dice score (0.32 vs 0.27; P = 0.048), with no observed statistical difference in sensitivity (0.79; P = 1.000). Conclusion Our findings demonstrate the potential of combining MRI and TRUS in a multimodal artificial intelligence (AI) model to improve localisation of clinically significant prostate cancer on TRUS images relative to single-modality models. These findings support further study of such multimodal AI models as an adjunct to MRI-TRUS fusion workflows.

title: Combined Host-Derived and Microbiological Biomarkers for the Detection of Peri-Implant Bone Loss: A Diagnostic Accuracy Study.
abstract: Aim To evaluate the diagnostic accuracy of host-derived and microbiological biomarkers, alone and in combination with clinical parameters, for the detection of peri-implant bone loss (BL). Methods A university-based cohort of subjects with dental implants was examined at baseline and after a mean follow-up of 3.9 years. Peri-implant BL served as the reference standard, defined as > 1 mm between baseline and follow-up radiographs; implants with < 0.5 mm BL served as controls. At follow-up, peri-implant crevicular fluid and submarginal-microbiological samples were collected. Bone metabolism and inflammatory biomarkers were quantified using Luminex technology. Bacterial loads were quantified by qPCR. Associations of biomarkers with BL were evaluated using multilevel logistic regression models. Diagnostic accuracy was assessed using ROC curves, with AUC, sensitivity, specificity, and predictive values reported. Results Seventy-one subjects with 273 implants were included. Twenty-eight exhibited peri-implant-BL > 1.0 mm over the follow-up period. Increased levels of IL-1β, T. denticola, Fusobacterium spp., and T. forsythia were associated with BL in unadjusted analyses. However, these associations were no longer statistically significant after adjustment for clinical parameters. Individual biomarkers demonstrated limited diagnostic accuracy (maximum AUC = 0.68). In contrast, biomarker combinations with clinical parameters exhibited excellent discriminative performance (AUC > 0.95). The combination of IL-1β and BoP-or-PPD achieved the highest accuracy (AUC = 0.97). Conclusions While individual biomarkers showed limited diagnostic utility, combining multiple predictors significantly improved the ability to detect peri-implant BL. Combining IL-1β with either BoP or PPD significantly outperformed individual clinical measures but did not outperform the combination of clinical parameters, highlighting the potential of integrated biomarker and clinical parameter approaches as screening tools for detecting BL.

title: Organ Wet Mount (Squash) Preparations in Fish Pathology: An Underused, Rapid and Low-Cost Tool for Tissue-Level Diagnosis During Necropsy.
abstract: Rapid, practical diagnostic approaches are essential for effective fish health management, yet cytological wet mount assessment of internal organs remains underused and inconsistently described in peer-reviewed aquatic veterinary literature. Organ wet mount (squash preparation) cytology offers a simple, low-cost method for immediate evaluation of fresh tissues. Unlike impression smears and aspirates, in which cells are assessed largely in isolation, squash preparations retain structural relationships within the tissue, providing tissue-level information at the point of examination that would otherwise await histopathology. The technique is widely applicable and requires minimal equipment, but guidance on its application beyond gill, skin, and fin samples is limited. A survey of fish health professionals confirmed that internal organ preparations are used less than external wet mounts. This review outlines the use of organ squash preparations during fish necropsy, emphasising technique, interpretation, and recognition of common findings rather than a comprehensive overview of disease. Key limitations, such as post-mortem changes, are discussed, as is the role of targeted special stains and follow-up diagnostics. Greater awareness and more consistent use of organ squash cytology have the potential to improve early detection of disease and support more targeted diagnostic decision-making in fish health investigations.

title: Outcome following lag screw fixation of non-C3 carpal slab fractures in horses.
abstract: Objective To describe clinical features and short- and long-term outcomes of horses treated with lag screw fixation of slab fractures of the radial carpal (Cr), intermediate carpal (Ci), ulnar carpal (Cu), second (C2) or fourth (C4) carpal bones. Study design Retrospective case study. Animals Horses (n = 19) treated with lag screw fixation for slab fractures of Cr, Ci, Cu, C2 or C4. Methods Medical records of patients with carpal slab fractures were reviewed, and those undergoing internal fixation of slab fractures involving Cr, Ci, Cu, C2, or C4 carpal bones from January 2008 to January 2026 were included. Long-term outcomes were obtained by a standardized questionnaire. Descriptive data are presented. Results Predominant breeds included Thoroughbreds (7/19) and Warmbloods (7/19). A total of 10 of 19 fractures were caused by traumatic falls, including six during recovery from general anesthesia. Five of 19 surgeries were performed with arthroscopic guidance, and 14/19 surgeries were performed with computed tomography (CT) guidance. Survival beyond 1 year was 88%, with 53% returning to previous athletic function and 71% owner satisfaction. Conclusion Prognosis for return to the previous level of work was good and comparable to that previously reported for internal fixation of C3 slab fractures. Clinical significance Lag screw fixation provides good outcomes in survival, return to work, and owner satisfaction for slab fractures of Cr, Ci, Cu, C2, or C4.

title: Endoscopic treatment strategies for gastric foveolar-type adenoma with a raspberry-like appearance.
abstract: Background/objectives Endoscopic treatment strategies for gastric foveolar-type adenoma with a raspberry-like appearance (GFA-R) have not yet been established. We aimed to clarify the efficacy and safety of endoscopic procedures for GFA-R. Methods We extracted GFA-Rs, which were pathologically diagnosed in accordance with WHO classification, at our hospital from January 2009 to December 2023 by endoscopy and retrospectively analyzed their clinicopathological features and endoscopic outcomes. Results Eighty-eight GFA-Rs were collected from 74 patients. The mean size of GFA-Rs was 4.2 mm (range, 1-10 mm). All lesions demonstrated intramucosal neoplasms without lymphovascular invasion. Endoscopic procedures included only biopsy (n=6), cold forceps polypectomy (CFP; n=42, as outpatient 38/42), cold snare polypectomy (CSP; n=4), endoscopic mucosal resection (EMR; n=36, as inpatient 36/36). The overall en bloc resection rate was 93.9 % (77/82), with rates of 92.9 % (39/42) for CFP, 75.0 % (3/4) for CSP, and 97.2 % (35/36) for EMR, respectively. Lesions smaller than 5 mm were more often treated with CFP while lesions larger than 5 mm were more often treated with EMR. No complications, such as post-operative bleeding or delayed perforation, occurred regardless of the endoscopic procedure. The mean follow-up period was 28.7 months (range, 2-165 months). No local recurrences occurred at 1 year (9-18 months) after an endoscopic procedure for 62 lesions, 2 years (19-30 months) for 40 lesions, and 3 years (31-42 months) for 24 lesions. Conclusions These results suggest that endoscopic procedures for GFA-R are effective and safe regardless of the procedure used. Moreover, outpatient CFP may be a simple, useful, and cost-effective endoscopic procedure for GFA-R smaller than 5 mm.

title: Deep Learning-Based 3D CT Body Composition Is Associated With Mortality in Patients Undergoing Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement.
abstract: Background Recent advances in artificial intelligence enable fully automated 3-dimensional computed tomography (CT)-based body composition quantification. We investigated whether automated CT-derived thoraco-abdominopelvic body composition measures are associated with mortality after transcatheter aortic valve replacement. Methods In this retrospective multicenter study, consecutive patients undergoing transcatheter aortic valve replacement with preprocedural CT imaging were included between 2014 and 2023. A deep learning-based pipeline performed automated 3-dimensional segmentation of thoraco-abdominopelvic noncontrast CT scans to quantify volumes (L/m 2 ) and attenuations (Hounsfield units) of subcutaneous adipose tissue, visceral adipose tissue, muscular adipose tissue, and lean skeletal muscle, indexed to body surface area. Associations with mortality were evaluated using Cox models and Harrell C statistics, adjusting for demographics (age, sex, body mass index) and cardiometabolic risk factors (hypertension, diabetes, chronic renal failure). Results Among 915 patients (median age, 84 years [interquartile range, 77-90]; 58% men), 160 (17.5%) died over a median follow-up of 22 months (interquartile range, 14-36). Restricted cubic spline analyses demonstrated that lower subcutaneous adipose tissue volume and higher adipose tissue attenuation were associated with increased mortality, whereas higher skeletal muscle volume and attenuation were associated with improved survival. Addition of body composition measures provided incremental discriminatory value beyond demographics and cardiometabolic risk factors (Harrell C, 0.66 versus 0.71; P <0.001). Conclusions Automated 3-dimensional CT-derived body composition measures provide independent prognostic information and improve risk stratification for mortality after transcatheter aortic valve replacement. Low subcutaneous adipose tissue volume and higher adipose tissue attenuation identify patients at increased risk, whereas higher skeletal muscle volume and attenuation are associated with lower mortality.

title: EXPRESS: Cerebral blood flow-oxygen metabolism uncoupling at 24 hours after stroke thrombectomy.
abstract: BackgroundFollowing successful endovascular therapy (EVT) for acute ischemic stroke, tissue with abnormal perfusion may have impaired oxygen extraction and metabolism. MRI model-based oxygen extraction fraction (OEFmax) and cerebral metabolic rate of oxygen (CMRO2) were characterized in hypoperfusion and hyperemia regions 24 hours post-EVT.MethodsEighty-four patients were included with anterior circulation vessel occlusion, successful recanalization, and an MRI at 24 hours post-EVT. Time-to-maximum (Tmax) and cerebral blood flow (CBF) were evaluated for hypoperfusion and hyperemia. CBF, OEFmax, and CMRO2 were quantified using i) segmentation-based and ii) single slice region of interest (ROI) analyses. Normalized CBF, OEFmax, and CMRO2 were calculated by dividing the segmentation or ROI value by the contralateral value.ResultsSixty-seven (80%) patients had abnormal perfusion; hypoperfusion in 22 (26%), hyperemia in 36 (43%), and both in 9 (11%). Compared to control, hypoperfused regions demonstrated a 62% CBF decrease, 52% CMRO2 decrease, and 68% OEFmax increase (p<0.01). Hyperemic regions demonstrated a 58% CBF increase, 26% CMRO2 increase, and 25% OEFmax decrease (p<0.01). Hyperemia had no significant correlation between normalized CBF and CMRO2 (p=0.14).ConclusionHyperemia regions demonstrated cerebral blood flow-oxygen metabolism uncoupling, suggesting the underlying mechanism as loss of cerebrovascular autoregulation rather than hypermetabolic demand.

title: Stroke-associated pneumonia: from immunodepression to bedside management and future research directions.
abstract: Stroke-associated pneumonia (SAP) is one of the most frequent complications after acute stroke, affecting approximately one in eight stroke patients. Besides prolonged hospitalisation and increased healthcare costs, it is also a major risk factor for mortality and poor functional recovery. The pathophysiology of SAP is driven by two converging processes: impaired local airway defence due to dysphagia as well as reduced airway clearance reflexes, and systemic stroke-induced immunodepression driven by dysfunction of the autonomic nervous system. While post-stroke immunodepression is a major risk factor for SAP, it might limit unwanted autoimmune responses within the brain. Conversely, SAP itself may drive neuroinflammation and contribute to post-stroke cognitive impairment. Despite its clinical importance, high-quality evidence to guide practice on prevention, diagnosis, and treatment of SAP remains scarce and guideline recommendations are mostly based on expert consensus. Diagnosis of SAP is suggested to be based on standardised clinical criteria supported by chest radiography and C-reactive protein as an adjunct where uncertainty persists. After diagnosis, guidelines suggest prompt empirical antibiotic therapy according to local protocols. In contrast, preventive antibiotics, even for high-risk patients, neither improve clinical outcome nor reduce SAP frequency. Currently recommended preventive strategies for SAP therefore mostly focus on dysphagia management and early mobilisation. This review integrates the pathophysiology, long-term consequences of SAP and further research directions based on the current knowledge on post-stroke immunology with prevention, diagnosis and treatment of SAP as set out in the recent European Stroke Organisation guideline and related guidelines.

title: Massive enlargement of a previously unrecognized bronchogenic cyst over 8 years with intracystic hemorrhage and complex surgical resection: a case report.
abstract: Background Bronchogenic cysts are usually asymptomatic and are often detected incidentally; however, they may become symptomatic due to infection, hemorrhage, or enlargement. We report a case of a previously unrecognized bronchogenic cyst that showed substantial enlargement from 4.8 to 13 cm over an 8-year interval, with intracystic hemorrhage, ultimately requiring partial resection of the esophageal muscularis. Case presentation A man in his 20s presented with upper abdominal pain and nausea. Computed tomography revealed a 13-cm mass extending from below the tracheal bifurcation to the level of the gastric cardia. A CT scan obtained eight years earlier during the evaluation of abdominal pain had shown a 4.8-cm cystic lesion below the tracheal bifurcation, demonstrating substantial enlargement over the intervening period. Although conservative treatment was attempted, compressive symptoms persisted; therefore, surgical resection was performed for definitive diagnosis and symptom relief. Severe inflammatory adhesions necessitated right open thoracotomy with partial resection of the esophageal muscularis. The cyst contained a large hematoma, and histopathological examination confirmed the diagnosis of a bronchogenic cyst with intracystic hemorrhage. Conclusion This case demonstrates substantial enlargement of a previously unrecognized bronchogenic cyst from 4.8 to 13 cm over an 8-year interval, with intracystic hemorrhage, symptomatic progression, and technically demanding surgical resection. The potential for substantial enlargement and increasing surgical complexity should be considered when determining the timing of resection for bronchogenic cysts.

title: Differential Trajectories of Brain Atrophy in Multiple Sclerosis, MOGAD, and AQP4 + NMOSD: The Role of Disease Activity in MOGAD.
abstract: Background and objectives Multiple sclerosis (MS), myelin oligodendrocyte glycoprotein antibody-associated disease (MOGAD), and aquaporin-4 antibody-positive neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder (AQP4 + NMOSD) are inflammatory demyelinating disorders with distinct mechanisms of tissue injury. MS is characterized by diffuse neurodegeneration, whereas damage in antibody-mediated diseases is considered attack related. In MOGAD, the relationship between disease activity and brain atrophy remains unclear. We aimed to compare longitudinal trajectories of global and regional brain atrophy across MS, MOGAD, and AQP4 + NMOSD and investigate whether atrophy in MOGAD is associated with disease course and lesion dynamics. Methods In this retrospective multicenter Magnetic Resonance Imaging in Multiple Sclerosis (MAGNIMS) study, patients fulfilling the following criteria were enrolled: (1) age 18 years or older, (2) MS/MOGAD/AQP4 + NMOSD diagnosis, (3) ≥2 same-scanner brain MRIs ≥6 months apart and ≥3 months postattack, (4) concurrent Expanded Disability Status Scale, and (5) disease course information. White matter lesions were segmented using the Lesion Segmentation Toolbox. Longitudinal brain volumes were quantified on lesion-filled T1-weighted images using Sequence Adaptive Multimodal SEGmentation (SAMSEG) with a within-subject template approach. In MOGAD, lesion dynamics were classified as stable/new lesions/lesion resolution. Linear mixed-effects models adjusted for age, sex, baseline volume, and center estimated atrophy rates. Results Overall, 489 participants from 15 centers were included (98 MS [mean age 39.79 years, 68.37% female], 72 MOGAD [42.14 years, 66.67%], 41 AQP4 + NMOSD [51.25 years, 87.80%], and 278 healthy controls [42.94 years, 61.87%]). The mean follow-up was MS: 2.44 ± 1.55 years, MOGAD: 2.57 ± 1.85, and AQP4 + NMOSD: 3.22 ± 2.42. Compared with controls, MS showed accelerated global brain atrophy (β = -2.027 cm 3 per year, 95% CI -3.430 to -0.623). MOGAD demonstrated white matter volume loss (β = -0.989, 95% CI -1.889 to -0.090) and ventricular enlargement (lateral: β = 0.219, 95% CI 0.089-0.350; third ventricle: β = 0.009, 95% CI 0.003-0.015). AQP4 + NMOSD showed pallidal volume reduction (β = -0.008, 95% CI -0.014 to -0.001). Within MOGAD, relapsing patients (62.5%) exhibited greater third ventricular expansion than MS (β = 0.009, 95% CI 0.001-0.017). MOGAD with new lesions (22.22%) had greater ventricular enlargement than controls (lateral: β = 0.359, 95% CI 0.147-0.572; third ventricle: β = 0.016, 95% CI 0.006-0.025), MS, and AQP4 + NMOSD. Discussion Each inflammatory demyelinating disease exhibits a characteristic pattern of brain atrophy. In MOGAD, neuroaxonal loss seems associated with inflammatory activity and lesion accrual, supporting an event-driven pattern of tissue injury rather than diffuse neurodegeneration. Limitations include small NMOSD sample, heterogeneous follow-up, and potential scanner-related variability.

title: Performance of<sup>68</sup>Ga-PSMA-11 PET/CT for Diagnosing Tumor Thrombus and Predicting Response to Pembrolizumab and Axitinib in Patients with Renal Cell Carcinoma: A Pilot, Retrospective Study.
abstract: Objectives To investigate the performance of 68 Ga-PSMA-11 PET/CT for diagnosing tumor thrombus (TT) and predicting response to pembrolizumab and axitinib in renal cell carcinoma (RCC) with TT. Methods We reviewed RCC patients who underwent contrast-enhanced CT, mpMRI, and 68 Ga-PSMA-11 PET/CT. Diagnostic performance for detecting TT was analyzed, with TT confirmed by experienced pathologists. We further analyzed clear cell RCC (ccRCC) patients with TT who received pembrolizumab and axitinib and evaluated imaging features for predicting therapeutic efficacy by using receiver operating characteristic analysis. Internal validation was performed using bootstrap resampling (1000 iterations). Model calibration was assessed with the Hosmer-Lemeshow test. Results A total of 166 RCC patients were initially included, of whom 56 had TT. 68 Ga-PSMA-11 PET/CT showed higher overall diagnostic performance for TT than contrast-enhanced CT and mpMRI, with incremental detection primarily observed for Mayo level 0-I TT. The sensitivity and specificity of PET/CT in diagnosing TT were 0.96 (95% CI 0.88-0.99) and 0.97 (95% CI 0.92-0.99), respectively. Then, 35 ccRCC patients with TT underwent an average of 5 cycles of pembrolizumab and axitinib, followed by surgery. Following neoadjuvant therapy, 21 patients exhibited a partial response, while 14 showed nonresponse. TT SUVmax demonstrated significant predictive value for response to neoadjuvant therapy, with an AUC of 0.80 (95% CI 0.63-0.92; bootstrap-corrected, 0.79). The Hosmer-Lemeshow test indicated adequate calibration (P > 0.05). Conclusions 68 Ga-PSMA-11 PET/CT may provide incremental value for detecting low-level TT and shows potential for predicting response to pembrolizumab plus axitinib in RCC. However, the clinical significance of detecting early TT remains uncertain.

title: Hydatid Pulmonary Embolism: A 25-Year Single-Center Case Series with Review of Current Management
abstract: Introduction: Hydatid pulmonary embolism is a rare but serious complication of cystic echinococcosis. It most often results from the rupture of a cardiac hydatid cyst into the right chambers or, more rarely, from the extension of a hepatic cyst into the inferior vena cava with embolic migration to the pulmonary arteries. Diagnosis is difficult due to non-specific clinical presentation. Methods We conducted a retrospective study including patients treated for hydatid pulmonary embolism in the thoracic and cardiovascular surgery department between 2000 and 2024. Clinical, radiological, therapeutic and evolutionary data were analysed. Results Nine patients were identified (5 women, 4 men), with a mean age of 39 years (19–64 years). All were symptomatic. The diagnosis was based on chest computed tomography and/or pulmonary angiography. The involvement was right-sided in six cases, left-sided in one case and bilateral in two cases. Six patients had an associated hepatic cyst and two had cardiac involvement. Eight patients underwent surgery (lobectomy, segmentectomy, pneumonectomy or embolectomy with cystectomy). One patient died before surgery due to compressive pericardial effusion. The average length of postoperative hospitalisation was four days, with no immediate complications. At follow-up (6 months to 7 years), the majority of patients were stable. One late death due to acute heart failure occurred at 12 months and one recurrence was observed at 7 years. Conclusion Hydatid pulmonary embolism is a rare condition with a potentially severe prognosis. Surgical treatment remains central. The role of adjuvant medical treatment with albendazole remains to be clarified.

title: Case Report: Primary hyperparathyroidism with intrathyroidal adenoma in a patient with systemic lupus erythematosus and antiphospholipid syndrome: The first case report
abstract: The occurrence of primary hyperparathyroidism (PHP) in patients with systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) is rare. The few cases reported parathyroid adenoma as the origin of PHP. We herein, report the first case of concomitant diagnosis of PHP with ectopic intrathyroidal adenoma and SLE associated with antiphospholipid syndrome (APS). A 43-years old woman presented with deep venous thrombosis (DVT) and pulmonary embolism (PE) medically treated. The etiological screening retained APS associated with SLE diagnosed. Other than that, biological tests revealed hypercalcemia, hypophosphatemia and elevated levels of parathyroid hormone (PTH) leading to the diagnosis of PHP. Cervical ultrasound and SPECT/CT parathyroid scintigraphy found a suspect thyroidal nodule with a pathological parathyroid gland. Thyroid lobectomy and isthmectomy histopathological examination revealed inferior intrathyroidal adenoma. Surgical intervention permitted to correct calcium-phosphate disturbances and to normalize PTH levels. Hypercalcemia in SLE patients should be roughly investigated. Even if PHP is a common cause of hypercalcemia in general population, it remains rare in SLE patients. In such cases, ectopic adenoma is exceptional.

title: The CBI-M framework for characterization of traumatic brain injury: Evaluation of performance using data from the CENTER-TBI and TRACK-TBI prospective cohort studies.
abstract: Background The CBI-M Framework, incorporating Clinical, Biomarker, Imaging, and Modifier pillars, was recently proposed to provide a comprehensive characterization of patients with acute traumatic brain injury (TBI). Such detailed characterization reflects the clinical and biological heterogeneity of TBI, and is considered essential to inform appropriate clinical management. Still unclear is the extent to which CBI-M captures clinically relevant heterogeneity in relation to diagnosis, clinical care pathways, and longer-term outcome. Prior to broad implementation into clinical practice and research, its diagnostic and prognostic performance needs to be ascertained. In this study, we aim to explore how CBI-M and its constituent pillars relate to diagnosis, clinical care pathways, and outcome in two large contemporary TBI cohorts. Methods and findings We analyzed data of patients with acute TBI enrolled in the European-based CENTER-TBI (N = 4,509) and US-based TRACK-TBI (N = 2,552) prospective observational studies. We assessed associations of the CBI-M Framework, its pillars, and pillar components with key clinical endpoints: diagnosis (traumatic intracranial injury on computed tomography); care pathways (hospital admission, intensive care admission, intracranial pressure monitoring, and major cranial surgery); and outcomes at 6 months post-injury (mortality, Glasgow Outcome Scale-Extended (GOSE), and health-related quality of life (HRQoL)). Discriminatory performance was calculated using the AUC and explained variability expressed with Nagelkerke's pseudo-R2. Prognostic performance was compared to the established IMPACT-Lab and CRASH-CT prediction models in their respective target populations. For diagnostic and care path endpoints full CBI-M models achieved excellent discrimination (AUC CENTER-TBI: from 0.83 to 0.95; TRACK-TBI: from 0.88 to 0.98), and high proportions of explained variability (pseudo-R2 CENTER-TBI: from 0.41 to 0.72; TRACK-TBI: from 0.55 to 0.80). Contributions of individual pillars varied by endpoint, with the Biomarker pillar contributing most for CT-defined abnormalities and the Imaging pillar to major cranial surgery. For mortality and unfavorable outcome (GOSE ≤ 4) similarly strong performance was observed: CENTER-TBI: AUC 0.89 (95% Confidence intervals (CI) [0.88,0.90]) and 0.92 (95% CI [0.91,0.94]) respectively; pseudo-R2 0.53 (95% CI [0.50,0.57]) and 0.55 (95% CI [0.51,0.59]) respectively; TRACK-TBI: AUC 0.91 (95% CI [0.89,0.93]) and 0.95 (95% CI [0.93,0.97]) respectively; pseudo-R2 0.57 (95% CI [0.52,0.62] and 0.57 (95% CI [0.50, 0.64] respectively), whereas performance for HRQoL was modest. Compared to the IMPACT-Lab and CRASH-CT models in their respective target populations, pseudo-R2 values suggest that the full CBI-M model was more strongly associated with 6-month mortality and unfavorable outcomes. Methodological limitations include the restriction to analysis of data from high-income settings, limiting generalizability, the absence of three elements of the modifier pillar in the datasets accessed, and risk of possible reverse causality in some analyses. Conclusions CBI-M provides a robust multimodal characterization of acute TBI that aligns closely with clinical decision-making and outcomes. Further prospective validation and optimization are justified and needed to inform implementation of the CBI-M Framework in clinical practice and research.

title: A white-light endoscopy-based mixed-effects nomogram for predicting small colorectal polyp neoplasia in resource-limited settings.
abstract: Introduction Accurate optical characterization of small colorectal polyps relies on narrow-band imaging (NBI) or artificial intelligence, both of which are unavailable in resource-limited settings. Objectives We aimed to develop and validate a web-based nomogram using white-light endoscopy (WLE) and routine clinical variables to predict neoplastic polyp histology. Patients and methods This prospective single-center study (Vietnam, September 2020-April 2021) included 301 patients with 451 small colorectal polyps (≤10 mm). Polyps were assessed in real time using WLE and NBI before histological confirmation. Data were split at the patient level into training (254 patients, 383 polyps) and validation (47 patients, 68 polyps) cohorts. L1-penalized generalized linear mixed-effects models were used for feature selection and model development. Results Neoplastic histology was present in 55.9% of polyps. Four predictors were identified: sessile/pedunculated morphology (0-Is/0-Ip), age ≥50 years, polyp size >5 mm, and neoplastic WLE diagnosis. In internal validation, the WLE+3F model achieved an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.849, outperforming WLE alone (AUC, 0.760; P = 0.009) and comparable with NBI (AUC, 0.858; P = 0.86), with sensitivity of 65.8%, specificity of 90.0%, and good calibration (Brier score, 0.160). Decision curve analysis showed clinical net benefit. Conclusions A WLE-based nomogram combined with 3 clinical factors achieved performance comparable with NBI, offering an accessible tool for real-time risk stratification in resource-limited settings; external validation is warranted.

Accurate optical characterization of small colorectal polyps relies on narrow-band imaging (NBI) or artificial intelligence, both of which are unavailable in resource-limited settings.

We aimed to develop and validate a web-based nomogram using white-light endoscopy (WLE) and routine clinical variables to predict neoplastic polyp histology.

This prospective single-center study (Vietnam, September 2020-April 2021) included 301 patients with 451 small colorectal polyps (≤10 mm). Data were split at the patient level into training (254 patients, 383 polyps) and validation (47 patients, 68 polyps) cohorts. Decision curve analysis showed clinical net benefit.

Conclusions

A WLE-based nomogram combined with 3 clinical factors achieved performance comparable with NBI, offering an accessible tool for real-time risk stratification in resource-limited settings; external validation is warranted.

title: From Manual to Machine: Development and Internal Validation of an NLP-Based Prediction Model for Brain Death Using Admission CT Reports, 2011–2024
abstract: BACKGROUND/OBJECTIVES: Early identification of patients progressing toward brain death may reduce missed organ donation opportunities. We aimed to develop and internally validate an interpretable natural language processing (NLP) model using admission brain computed tomog-raphy (CT) reports. METHODS: This single-center retrospective cohort included 163 adults ad-mitted between 2011 and 2024 with acute neurological injury; 96 subsequently fulfilled brain death criteria and 67 did not. Predictors were derived exclusively from admission CT report text using rule-based preprocessing and term frequency–inverse document frequency word 1–3-gram features. Logistic regression, random forest, XGBoost, and support vector machine models were evaluated using repeated stratified 5-fold cross-validation with 20 repetitions. Vectorization, cal-ibration, model fitting, and threshold selection were restricted to training folds. A prespecified sensitivity target of at least 95% guided threshold selection. Interpretability was assessed using SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP). RESULTS: XGBoost achieved the highest discrimination, with a mean area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.807 (95% confidence in-terval, 0.793–0.820) and a pooled out-of-fold value of 0.791. At the high-sensitivity operating point, mean sensitivity was 0.947 and specificity was 0.275. SHAP identified clinically plausible descriptors related to cerebral edema, mass effect, ventricular distortion, ischemic injury, and midline abnormalities. CONCLUSIONS: Admission CT reports contain prognostic information that can be extracted using NLP to support earlier identification of patients at risk of progression to brain death and potential organ donation. External multicenter validation is required before clinical implementation.

title: Study on the Value of pH-Responsive Probes in Evaluating Acidic Environment Changes During Chronic Liver Disease Progression in Rats
abstract: During the progression of chronic liver disease, changes in the acidic microenvironment of liver tissue are closely correlated with the extent of pathological injury, making precise monitoring of these changes critical for disease assessment. Traditional detection methods (e.g., blood gas analysis, tissue pH electrodes) suffer from limitations such as high invasiveness and low spatiotemporal resolution, hindering dynamic reflection of hepatic acid environment evolution. PH-responsive probes (e.g., fluorescent probes, magnetic resonance probes), leveraging their non-invasive, real-time, and high-specificity advantages, have emerged as a research focus in this field. This review focuses on the application of such probes in rat chronic liver disease models: outlining their design principles and types, analyzing their quantitative detection capabilities for liver acidification levels, summarizing their value in correlating pathological processes such as liver inflammation, fibrosis, and cirrhosis, and demonstrating their ability to identify disease progression and evaluate intervention efficacy through early detection of acidic environment changes. Studies indicate that pH-responsive probes provide a tool for elucidating the mechanisms of the acidic microenvironment in chronic liver disease and lay the foundation for developing non-invasive monitoring technologies in clinical translation, holding significant academic and practical value.

title: Proximal Scaphoid Pole Reconstruction Utilizing Ipsilateral Proximal Hamate Autograft.
abstract: Background Proximal pole scaphoid fractures complicated by nonunion and osteonecrosis present a challenging scenario with few good reconstructive options, especially when the proximal fragment is small or fragmented 1-4 . The use of an ipsilateral proximal hamate osteochondral autograft has emerged as a promising technique for reconstructing the proximal scaphoid pole, with the potential to restore carpal mechanics while avoiding the morbidity associated with free vascularized bone grafts or distant autograft sites. Description The procedure involves replacing the diseased proximal scaphoid with a structurally matched osteochondral graft from the ipsilateral proximal hamate. After excising the necrotic or fragmented scaphoid pole, a size-matched graft-harvested with its attached volar capitohamate ligament-is rotated 180° on its longitudinal axis to replicate normal scaphoid anatomy. The defect is measured in 3 planes using the scapholunate joint (proximal) and viable distal scaphoid surface as boundaries. On the hamate, an osteotomy is marked 8 to 10 mm distal to its proximal tip, parallel to the articular surface. The volar capitohamate ligament is preserved to guide graft orientation and maintain stability. These measurements align with recent anatomic and biomechanical studies that have confirmed 6 to 10-mm grafts accurately reproduce scaphoid morphology without compromising carpal kinematics. The graft is then inserted into the defect and secured with rigid internal fixation (headless compression screws or Kirschner wires). Residual gaps may be filled with cancellous bone graft. Scapholunate interosseous ligament (SLIL) reconstruction is typically performed by suturing the hamate's volar capitohamate ligament to the dorsal SLIL remnant on the lunate with a 2-0 nonabsorbable suture. In patients with a partially intact SLIL, such as after failed fixation, the hamate graft alone may provide adequate stability, making formal reconstruction unnecessary. If intraoperative findings reveal dorsal scapholunate instability or an attenuated SLIL, reconstruction is indicated. Healthy, tensionable ligament remnants are repaired directly or reinforced with suture anchors. When dorsal fibers are deficient but volar remnants remain, the attached volar capitohamate ligament is used for reinforcement. For small defects, a micro-interference screw may be employed for fixation. Postoperatively, the wrist is immobilized in a cast. When radiographic evidence of union is observed, the cast is removed and the patient begins a structured hand therapy program. Alternatives Alternatives include vascularized and nonvascularized bone grafts (e.g., iliac crest), a vascularized medial femoral trochlear osteochondral flap, costochondral rib graft, proximal row carpectomy, and wrist arthrodesis 1,2 . These may be limited by donor-site morbidity, complexity, or suboptimal restoration of wrist biomechanics. Rationale The articular surface of the proximal hamate closely matches the curvature and size of the proximal pole of the scaphoid, making it an ideal structural substitute. The use of an articular autograft from the same wrist avoids the need for distant donor sites and microsurgical anastomoses, reducing overall morbidity. Additionally, because the graft is harvested with its volar ligament attached, it enables a simultaneous SLIL reconstruction, addressing carpal instability in a way that standard bone grafts cannot. This technique is relatively straightforward and reproducible, and it is especially beneficial in young, active patients with an irreparable proximal scaphoid, offering a chance to heal the nonunion and preserve near-normal wrist function without resorting to salvage procedures. Expected outcomes Radiographic union is expected in the majority of cases within 8 to 12 weeks. Published series have demonstrated union rates of >90%, improved pain, restoration of near-normal wrist kinematics, and substantial improvements in range of motion and grip strength, although not always to the level of the contralateral wrist. Complications are rare but include nonunion, donor-site pain, and persistent stiffness. Background

Proximal pole scaphoid fractures complicated by nonunion and osteonecrosis present a challenging scenario with few good reconstructive options, especially when the proximal fragment is small or fragmented1-4. The use of an ipsilateral proximal hamate osteochondral autograft has emerged as a promising technique for reconstructing the proximal scaphoid pole, with the potential to restore carpal mechanics while avoiding the morbidity associated with free vascularized bone grafts or distant autograft sites.

Description

The procedure involves replacing the diseased proximal scaphoid with a structurally matched osteochondral graft from the ipsilateral proximal hamate. After excising the necrotic or fragmented scaphoid pole, a size-matched graft-harvested with its attached volar capitohamate ligament-is rotated 180° on its longitudinal axis to replicate normal scaphoid anatomy. The defect is measured in 3 planes using the scapholunate joint (proximal) and viable distal scaphoid surface as boundaries. On the hamate, an osteotomy is marked 8 to 10 mm distal to its proximal tip, parallel to the articular surface. The volar capitohamate ligament is preserved to guide graft orientation and maintain stability. These measurements align with recent anatomic and biomechanical studies that have confirmed 6 to 10-mm grafts accurately reproduce scaphoid morphology without compromising carpal kinematics. The graft is then inserted into the defect and secured with rigid internal fixation (headless compression screws or Kirschner wires). Residual gaps may be filled with cancellous bone graft. Scapholunate interosseous ligament (SLIL) reconstruction is typically performed by suturing the hamate's volar capitohamate ligament to the dorsal SLIL remnant on the lunate with a 2-0 nonabsorbable suture. In patients with a partially intact SLIL, such as after failed fixation, the hamate graft alone may provide adequate stability, making formal reconstruction unnecessary. If intraoperative findings reveal dorsal scapholunate instability or an attenuated SLIL, reconstruction is indicated. Healthy, tensionable ligament remnants are repaired directly or reinforced with suture anchors. When dorsal fibers are deficient but volar remnants remain, the attached volar capitohamate ligament is used for reinforcement. For small defects, a micro-interference screw may be employed for fixation. Postoperatively, the wrist is immobilized in a cast. When radiographic evidence of union is observed, the cast is removed and the patient begins a structured hand therapy program.

Alternatives

Alternatives include vascularized and nonvascularized bone grafts (e.g., iliac crest), a vascularized medial femoral trochlear osteochondral flap, costochondral rib graft, proximal row carpectomy, and wrist arthrodesis1,2. These may be limited by donor-site morbidity, complexity, or suboptimal restoration of wrist biomechanics.

Rationale

The articular surface of the proximal hamate closely matches the curvature and size of the proximal pole of the scaphoid, making it an ideal structural substitute. The use of an articular autograft from the same wrist avoids the need for distant donor sites and microsurgical anastomoses, reducing overall morbidity. Additionally, because the graft is harvested with its volar ligament attached, it enables a simultaneous SLIL reconstruction, addressing carpal instability in a way that standard bone grafts cannot. This technique is relatively straightforward and reproducible, and it is especially beneficial in young, active patients with an irreparable proximal scaphoid, offering a chance to heal the nonunion and preserve near-normal wrist function without resorting to salvage procedures.

Radiographic union is expected in the majority of cases within 8 to 12 weeks. Published series have demonstrated union rates of >90%, improved pain, restoration of near-normal wrist kinematics, and substantial improvements in range of motion and grip strength, although not always to the level of the contralateral wrist. title: All-Suture Fixation for Acute Turf Toe Injuries.
abstract: Background Turf toe is a hallux metatarsophalangeal joint (MTPJ) injury caused by hyperextension of the great toe with axial loading 1,2 . High-grade injuries may threaten return to sport and require surgery 3,4 . Here, we describe a capsular reconstruction of the great toe MTPJ with all-knotless suture anchors and suture tape augmentation for turf toe injuries, in isolation or in combination with a traumatic bunion, designed to reduce suture burden, minimize soft-tissue irritation, and facilitate recovery. Description The procedure begins with the patient supine. A direct medial approach to the hallux MTPJ is performed. Both the medial base of the proximal phalanx and the medial eminence of the metatarsal head are drilled at isometric points, and augmentation with suture tape is then performed. Isometric drill holes are placed in the medial proximal phalanx base and metatarsal head for suture tape augmentation. A knotless suture anchor is placed approximately 3 mm proximal to the articular margin of the metatarsal head, repairing the medial capsule in a horizontal mattress fashion. An additional knotless anchor is placed at the plantar plate insertion, and the suture is passed through the tibial sesamoid sling and tensioned with the toe in 20° of plantar flexion. Suture tape is secured into the proximal phalanx with an interference screw, then passed through the deep capsule into the metatarsal head, followed by the placement of an additional interference screw into the metatarsal head. The anchor is inserted into the plantar-medial proximal phalanx at the flexor hallucis brevis insertion. The toe is flexed during tensioning, then adjusted per clinical examination and the sesamoid location beneath the metatarsal head. Knotless fixation permits incremental tensioning with intraoperative assessment of motion. Final tensioning is performed with the toe in neutral to correct deformity without overconstraint, preserving range of motion. Alternatives Nonoperative alternatives include rest, ice, compression and elevation; anti-inflammatory drugs; activity modification; and brief immobilization 5,6 . Operative alternatives include primary capsuloligamentous complex repair with nonabsorbable sutures, plantar plate advancement with bone tunnels or suture anchors if primary repair is not feasible, and concomitant procedures such as sesamoidectomy and bunionectomy based on the injury pattern 2,7,8 . Rationale This technique is intended for high-grade turf toe injuries with capsuloligamentous disruption, sesamoid complex insufficiency, and MTPJ instability. Nonoperative treatment may be appropriate in cases of low-grade injury; however, persistent pain, instability, or loss of push-off strength following nonoperative treatment would indicate a higher-grade injury. Compared with isolated repair or plantar plate advancement alone, this technique restores both static and dynamic stabilizers of the hallux MTPJ while addressing associated angular deformity. Suture tape augmentation resists recurrent hyperextension and valgus forces while allowing controlled physiologic motion. Knotless, low-profile suture anchors minimize bulk and hardware prominence in a region with limited soft-tissue coverage and bone stock. This construct offers a robust reconstruction option for athletes requiring predictable restoration of stability and reliable return to sport. Expected outcomes Operative treatment of high-grade turf toe injuries has been shown to result in reliable pain relief, restored stability, and high rates of return to sport 8 . Previous studies have suggested improved function and earlier return to play compared with prolonged nonoperative treatment in appropriate patients 6,7 . Knotless suture anchors reduce implant prominence and eliminate knot-related irritation, while the small insertional diameter of the suture anchors preserves bone stock in the metatarsal head and proximal phalanx. This construct provides immediate stability while allowing controlled motion, facilitating rehabilitation, and reducing postoperative stiffness. Athletes typically return to unrestricted activity within 6 to 9 months, aided by the suture tape augmentation allowing earlier movement through the range of motion. This augmentation reduces the need for long-term spica splinting and bracing and reduces the risk of recurrence. Important tips The small anchor diameter and use of suture tape allow easy access without hardware burden.○ Suture choice depends on surgeon preference regarding construct stiffness and on the tissue quality and risk of irritation. We believe that suture tape lays flatter and, if required, knots are smaller.Avoid suture twisting or kinking, which can prematurely lock anchors, compromising fixation.○ After the anchor is placed, we keep the suture tape secured out of the field as we prepare the capsule with absorbable suture. As we load the second anchor, we maintain tension on the tape to prevent twisting.Overtightening the MTPJ capsule may lead to altered biomechanics. title: Surgical difficulty and factors associated with conversion to thoracotomy after neoadjuvant chemoimmunotherapy for non-small cell lung cancer: a single- center retrospective study
abstract: Abstract Background: Neoadjuvant chemoimmunotherapy can produce substantial tumor regression in resectable or potentially resectable non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), but treatment-related inflammation, fibrosis, and hilar adhesions may increase technical surgical difficulty. Methods: We retrospectively analyzed 101 patients with NSCLC who underwent surgery after neoadjuvant chemoimmunotherapy at a single center. Thirty-four patients completed video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery (VATS) and 67 underwent conversion to thoracotomy. Results: In the principal Firth penalized multivariable analysis, cT3-4 disease (OR 34.33, 95% CI 7.84–150.22), pulmonary artery relationship grade (OR 2.03 per grade, 95% CI 1.09–3.79), and bronchial relationship grade (OR 3.25 per grade, 95% CI 1.35–7.82) were associated with conversion. The cT3-4 estimate should be interpreted cautiously because of sparse non-conversion observations. Pulmonary artery and bronchial grades were also associated with longer operative time. Conversion was associated with longer operative time, greater blood loss, and longer chest tube duration, whereas no statistically significant differences were observed in R0 resection or pulmonary complication rates. Conclusions: Higher clinical T stage and more complex pulmonary artery and bronchial relationships on CT were associated with conversion and technical surgical difficulty after neoadjuvant chemoimmunotherapy. Preoperative assessment of local tumor extent and hilar anatomy may assist operative planning; conversion should be interpreted as a potential intraoperative safety strategy rather than automatically as failure of minimally invasive surgery.

title: Development and validation of a three-marker urine DNA methylation assay complementary to mpMRI for pre-biopsy risk stratification of clinically significant prostate cancer
abstract: Abstract Background Current prostate cancer (PCa) diagnostic strategies remain limited in accurately identifying clinically significant disease while avoiding unnecessary biopsy. This study aimed to develop and independently validate a non-invasive urine DNA methylation assay using naturally voided, non-digital rectal examination (non-DRE) urine and assess its complementary value with multiparametric magnetic resonance imaging (mpMRI) for detecting clinically significant prostate cancer (csPCa; Grade Group ≥ 2). Methods The biomarker discovery phase was initiated using microarray-based DNA methylation profiling to screen for tumor-specific alterations, and the candidate regions were subsequently validated by bisulfite-pyrosequencing in the same tissue specimens. Three prioritized markers– CDYL , EMX2 , and LRRC4– were incorporated into a linear target enrichment quantitative methylation-specific PCR assay. Marker-specific thresholds optimized in a training cohort (n = 33) were locked and evaluated in an independent validation cohort of men undergoing biopsy for suspected PCa (n = 97). All participants underwent pre-biopsy mpMRI and standard prostate biopsy. Of the 97 validation patients, 89 were evaluable for combined-modality analysis, while 8 were excluded due to missing mpMRI scans. Results In the training cohort, the assay achieved 100% sensitivity and 31.6% specificity for csPCa. In the independent validation cohort, standalone assay performance yielded 75.9% sensitivity and 44.2% specificity. Among the 89 patients evaluable for both modalities (49 csPCa, 40 no-csPCa), mpMRI alone (PI-RADS ≥ 4) showed a sensitivity of 69.4%. Combining the urine assay and mpMRI using an either-positive strategy significantly increased diagnostic sensitivity to 91.8% ( P < 0.01 vs. mpMRI alone), with a negative predictive value of 78.9%. In an exploratory analysis of the indeterminate PI-RADS 3 subgroup, the urine assay correctly identified all 4 biopsy-confirmed cases of csPCa (100% sensitivity). Conclusions The three-marker non-DRE urine DNA methylation assay demonstrates independent diagnostic performance and complementarity to mpMRI. Integrating this molecular assay with anatomical imaging significantly enhances csPCa detection compared with mpMRI alone. These findings support prospective evaluation of predefined, integrated MRI-urine methylation algorithms to refine pre-biopsy risk stratification and optimize biopsy decision-making.

title: Longitudinal intratumoral and peritumoral MRI radiomics for predicting pathologic complete response to neoadjuvant chemoimmunotherapy in locally advanced head and neck squamous cell carcinoma: a retrospective two-center study
abstract: Abstract Background Pathologic complete response (pCR) after neoadjuvant chemoimmunotherapy (NACI) is an important marker of treatment sensitivity in locally advanced head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC), but reliable preoperative prediction remains challenging. This study investigated whether longitudinal intratumoral and peritumoral MRI radiomics could improve pCR prediction and whether integration with clinicopathologic factors provided additional value. Methods This retrospective two-center study included 310 patients with locally advanced HNSCC who underwent NACI followed by definitive surgery, comprising 151 patients in the training cohort, 66 in the internal validation cohort, and 93 in the independent external test cohort. MRI was performed before treatment and after the second NACI cycle. Radiomic features were extracted from contrast-enhanced fat-suppressed T1-weighted images within the primary tumor and 1-, 3-, and 5-mm peritumoral regions. Features were selected using reproducibility assessment, correlation analysis, and least absolute shrinkage and selection operator regression. Pre-treatment intratumoral, on-treatment intratumoral, longitudinal intratumoral, multiscale longitudinal peritumoral, spatiotemporal radiomics, and clinical-spatiotemporal radiomics models were sequentially developed. Performance was evaluated using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), calibration analysis, decision curve analysis, and incremental discrimination metrics. Results Overall, 124 of 310 patients (40.0%) achieved pCR. The clinical-spatiotemporal radiomics model (M6), integrating histologic grade, combined positive score, longitudinal intratumoral features, and 3-mm longitudinal peritumoral features, showed the highest observed discrimination. The AUCs were 0.928 (95% CI, 0.882–0.974), 0.856 (95% CI, 0.749–0.963), and 0.864 (95% CI, 0.780–0.948) in the training, internal validation, and external test cohorts, respectively. In the external test cohort, sensitivity was 0.857 and specificity was 0.845. M6 also showed favorable calibration and net benefit across a broad range of threshold probabilities. Conclusions Integrating longitudinal intratumoral and peritumoral MRI radiomics with clinicopathologic factors improved preoperative prediction of pCR after NACI in locally advanced HNSCC. The model showed consistent performance in independent external testing and may support individualized pCR risk stratification, warranting further prospective multicenter validation.

title: ‘One shunt fits all?’: A comparative laboratory study of antibiotic- impregnated shunt catheters with retrospective clinical correlation
abstract: Abstract Introduction: Several antibiotic-impregnated shunt catheters are commercially available, but direct comparative data on their biochemical and physical characteristics remain limited. Previous observations from our single-centre neurosurgical unit suggested that nominally similar catheter types may be associated with different rates of otherwise unexplained abdominal pain. We therefore conducted a prospective comparative study to investigate potential biochemical and physical differences between commercially available antibiotic-impregnated shunt catheters. Methods: Ares®, Bactiseal® and XABO® catheters were compared for antibiotic content, rifampicin degradation products, elution characteristics and antimicrobial activity. Antibiotic elution was assessed during continuous saline perfusion at 20 mL/h and 37°C over 8 weeks, while antimicrobial activity against Staphylococcus epidermidis was evaluated over 60 days. Catheter dimensions, elastic modulus and surface morphology were assessed using three-dimensional computed tomography, nanoindentation and scanning electron microscopy, respectively. An exploratory retrospective quality-improvement dataset from our single-centre unit was additionally analysed to compare the frequency of otherwise unexplained abdominal pain between catheter types. Results: The three catheter systems showed product-specific differences in antibiotic content, rifampicin degradation profiles, elution characteristics, antimicrobial activity, dimensions, mechanical properties and surface morphology. XABO® most closely matched the declared antibiotic concentrations and retained the greatest proportion of intact rifampicin, while Ares® demonstrated the highest sustained clindamycin elution. All three catheters retained measurable activity against Staphylococcus epidermidis for 60 days, with XABO® showing the largest numerical inhibition zones throughout. In the 395-patient retrospective clinical analysis, otherwise unexplained abdominal pain was recorded in 90/182 patients with Ares® catheters (49.5%) compared with 12/108 patients with Bactiseal® catheters (11.1%). After adjustment for age, sex, primary diagnosis, modified Rankin Scale score and activity level, Ares® remained associated with greater odds of abdominal pain than Bactiseal® (adjusted OR 6.89, 95% CI 2.58–18.43; p<0.001). Conclusion: Commercially available antibiotic-impregnated shunt catheters showed product-specific biochemical and physical variation, while catheter type was associated with different rates of otherwise unexplained abdominal pain in a retrospective single-centre analysis. These findings are hypothesis-generating and do not establish causality or clinical superiority. Prospective multicentre studies are required to determine whether catheter-specific properties translate into clinically meaningful differences and should influence individualised shunt selection.

title: Bounded Repair Reachability of Residual Critical Blocks in 3D Binary Masks under SAFE-Gated Single-Voxel Flips
abstract: Abstract Critical configurations in three-dimensional binary images violate digital well-composedness, and voxel repairs can conflict with path constraints and foreground preservation. We formulate bounded repair reachability under single-voxel flips preserving the homotopy type of the foreground complex. We establish relations among admissible path sets and show that, under flip-once, endpoint and pathwise fidelity yield identical successful instances and shortest successful depths. Breadth-first search distinguishes found repairs, bounded absence and resource-limited outcomes. On 680 residual blocks from 222 Brain Tumor Segmentation (BraTS) 2021 masks, unrestricted searches within radius 2 and depth 6 find repairs for 72 blocks under endpoint fidelity and 15 under pathwise fidelity. An endpoint-faithful witness temporarily removes and restores input foreground; a completed search excludes pathwise-faithful repair of that block within these bounds. These results distinguish the topological validity of moves from the admissibility of repair paths. Conclusions are limited to the stated windows, horizons and moves.

title: ASFNR Clinical State of Practice Statement on Imaging of Chronic Subdural Hematoma.
abstract: Background The efficacy of middle meningeal artery embolization (MMAE) for chronic subdural hematoma (cSDH) has heightened interest in imaging biomarkers that may reflect neomembrane activity, predict recurrence, and identify patients most likely to benefit from treatment. Characterization of hematoma internal architecture, referred to as the imaging phenotype, may provide indirect information regarding the biological activity and maturation of the neomembrane. However, imaging phenotype has not been incorporated into randomized trials or validated treatment-selection algorithms, and standardized definitions and reporting remain lacking. Methods The American Society of Functional Neuroradiology Clinical Practice Committee developed this State of Practice statement through expert consensus and review of the available literature. Key message Noncontrast CT (NCCT) remains the primary imaging modality for cSDH assessment. Hematoma burden should be characterized by maximum thickness measured perpendicular to the inner table, midline shift, and, when appropriate, volume. Volume may be estimated using the ABC/2 formula, whereas segmentation is more accurate for irregular, crescentic, or multiloculated collections when available. Internal architecture should be described using the Nakaguchi framework of homogeneous, laminar, separated, and trabecular phenotypes, with mixed or transitional features explicitly reported. Advanced techniques, including dual-energy CT, photon-counting CT, MRI, and arterial spin labeling, may provide information regarding membrane activity but are supported by limited, largely single-center evidence and currently have a problem-solving rather than routine role. Standardized reporting and prospective validation are needed before imaging phenotype or advanced-imaging biomarkers can guide treatment selection.
originalAbstract:
Background

The efficacy of middle meningeal artery embolization (MMAE) for chronic subdural hematoma (cSDH) has heightened interest in imaging biomarkers that may reflect neomembrane activity, predict recurrence, and identify patients most likely to benefit from treatment. Characterization of hematoma internal architecture, referred to as the imaging phenotype, may provide indirect information regarding the biological activity and maturation of the neomembrane. However, imaging phenotype has not been incorporated into randomized trials or validated treatment-selection algorithms, and standardized definitions and reporting remain lacking.

Methods

The American Society of Functional Neuroradiology Clinical Practice Committee developed this State of Practice statement through expert consensus and review of the available literature.

Key message

Noncontrast CT (NCCT) remains the primary imaging modality for cSDH assessment. Hematoma burden should be characterized by maximum thickness measured perpendicular to the inner table, midline shift, and, when appropriate, volume. Volume may be estimated using the ABC/2 formula, whereas segmentation is more accurate for irregular, crescentic, or multiloculated collections when available. Internal architecture should be described using the Nakaguchi framework of homogeneous, laminar, separated, and trabecular phenotypes, with mixed or transitional features explicitly reported. Advanced techniques, including dual-energy CT, photon-counting CT, MRI, and arterial spin labeling, may provide information regarding membrane activity but are supported by limited, largely single-center evidence and currently have a problem-solving rather than routine role. Standardized reporting and prospective validation are needed before imaging phenotype or advanced-imaging biomarkers can guide treatment selection.

title: Preoperative apical margin risk estimation from T2-weighted MRI radiomics in prostate cancer with MRI-visible apical tumors: toward multidisciplinary decision support.
abstract: This retrospective study developed and validated a T2-weighted imaging (T2WI)-based radiomics model for preoperative prediction of apical positive surgical margins (PSMs) in patients undergoing radical prostatectomy for prostate cancer. Overall, 235 patients (74 with apical PSMs and 161 without apical PSMs) were randomly divided into a training set (n = 164; 69.8%) and an independent test set (n = 71; 30.2%). Eligible patients had preoperative multiparametric magnetic resonance imaging within 6 weeks before surgery, an index lesion involving or abutting the prostatic apex, definitive apical margin status, and standard radical prostatectomy without nerve-sparing. Patients with inadequate imaging for apical assessment or region-of-interest delineation, prior transurethral resection of the prostate, or neoadjuvant androgen-deprivation therapy were excluded. A total of 1409 radiomic features were extracted from T2WI. After normalization and removal of highly correlated features (|r| > 0.99), six optimal features were selected by recursive feature elimination. A gradient boosting machine model was constructed, and performance was assessed using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), Brier score, and decision curve analysis. The apical PSM rate was 31.5%. In the test set, the model achieved an AUC of 0.874, Brier score of 0.120, accuracy of 87.3%, sensitivity of 81.8%, and specificity of 89.8%. Skewness was the most important feature, contributing 34.8% to the model. Apical PSMs were significantly associated with extraprostatic extension (P = 0.001), and the tumor-margin model provided the greatest net clinical benefit. T2WI-based radiomics may support individualized preoperative risk assessment and surgical planning for prostate cancer.
